# Agent.bx
> **Most agents use Agent.yaml instead**
>
> The default way to define an agent is a plain [`Agent.yaml`](/conventions/agent-yaml/index.html). Reach for `Agent.bx` when the definition itself needs code: hooks, dynamic instructions, tools registered in code, an overridden method, or `detectEnvironment()`. A folder holds one or the other, never both. The sections on [the model slug](#the-model-slug), [environment overrides](#environment-overrides), [merge semantics](#merge-semantics) and [the always-on agent route](#the-always-on-agent-route) below apply to both.

`Agent.bx` is the advanced way to define an agent. A BxAgents project needs an `Agent.yaml` **or** an `Agent.bx`. It **extends bx-ai's own [`AiAgent`](https://ai.ortusbooks.com/main-components/agents/class-based-agents)** , so it *is* the agent - the build instantiates it rather than rebuilding one from a config struct, so what you write is what runs. Inherit and add whatever you need: private helpers, overridden methods, tools registered in code. Because it's a real class rather than a struct-returning descriptor, an IDE can introspect it like any other BoxLang class - jump to definition, autocomplete on inherited methods, the works.

```javascript
class extends="bxModules.bxai.models.runnables.AiAgent" {

	function init() {
		super.init(
			name        : "my-agent",
			description : "A helpful assistant",
			instructions: "You are a helpful assistant.",
			model       : aiModel( provider: "openai", params: { model: "gpt-5" } )
		)
		return this
	}

}
```

`bxAgents new --class` scaffolds exactly this shape (without `--class`, `new` scaffolds an `Agent.yaml`). `instructions.md` is optional - set `instructions` directly in `super.init()`, or drop the file beside `Agent.bx` and let the build wire it in for you (see the table below).

## What the build layers on top of the class
> **The rule:** an explicitly declared convention wins; otherwise the class is in charge.

So an agent that sets everything in its own `init()` gets nothing imposed on it, while one that sets the bare minimum still picks up the conventions it didn't speak for. Everything below is **optional** - declare a `configure()` returning any of these keys to override what the class itself set, or the matching `instructions.md`/`tools/`/`subagents/` convention folder:

|                    You declare                    |                                         The build emits                                         |                                                                 If you don't declare it                                                                  |
|---------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `instructions.md`                                 | `withInstructions( fileRead( ... ) )`                                                           | the class's own instructions stand                                                                                                                       |
| `model` in `configure()`                          | `setModel( aiModel( ... ) )`                                                                    | the class's own model stands                                                                                                                             |
| `name` / `description` in `configure()`           | `setName()` / `setDescription()`                                                                | the class's own stand                                                                                                                                    |
| `memory` in `configure()`                         | `setMemory( ... )`                                                                              | the class's own stands                                                                                                                                   |
| the `tools/` folder                               | `withTools( ... )` with that folder's tools                                                     | always - `withTools()` **appends** in bx-ai rather than replacing, so tools your class registered itself are kept and the agent's own `tools/` are added |
| `tools` / `toolOptions` in `configure()`          | `withTools( ... )` with each `item@module` / `*@module` listed, built with the module's options | no module tools; see [Tools](/conventions/agent-yaml/index.html#tools) and [Tool options](/conventions/agent-yaml/index.html#tool-options)               |
| `subAgents` on the class, or `subagents/` on disk | `addSubAgent( ... )` per child                                                                  | appended the same way                                                                                                                                    |
| `checkpointer` in `configure()`                   | `withCheckpointer( ... )`                                                                       | **injected anyway** if the class set none - see below                                                                                                    |

> **Info**
>
> The checkpointer is the one thing the build fills in unasked. An agent reachable from a gateway with no checkpointer has *silently* broken human-in-the-loop, so a class that set none still gets the `cache` default. A class that sets its own is left alone.
> **Warning**
>
> Deliberately **not** implemented by comparing your instance against bx-ai's `DEFAULT_AGENT_*` values. "Did the author mean this, or is it just the default?" is unanswerable, and an author who genuinely wanted the default name would find it silently replaced. Presence of an external declaration is a fact; intent behind a default value is not.

The class is copied into the generated app at `agent/classes/` and instantiated there by its own absolute file path (never a relative lookup that would depend on a registered mapping), exactly as `tools/`, `skills/` and `mcp/` are copied - so a packaged `.bxa` carries it, and `chat`/`invoke`/`serve` all instantiate it the same way whether or not a real ColdBox container is booted.

## `configure()` (optional) - overriding what the class set

A `configure()` method is entirely optional. Declare it only to override specific fields from outside the class - useful for keeping deployment-specific values (a different model per environment, say) out of the class body itself:

```javascript
class extends="bxModules.bxai.models.runnables.AiAgent" {

	function init() {
		super.init(
			name  : "with-mcp-servers-agent",
			model : aiModel( provider: "openai", params: { model: "gpt-5" } )
		)
		return this
	}

	function configure() {
		return {
			mcpServers : [
				"https://example.com/mcp",
				{ url : "https://other.com/mcp", name : "other" }
			]
		};
	}

}
```

|                                                                               Field                                                                                |       Type       |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `name`                                                                                                                                                             | string           | Also becomes this agent's `config/WireBox.bx` binding key at build time (`getInstance( name )`, or `agent( name )` in a scheduler) - see [schedules/](/conventions/schedules/index.html) - so it must be unique across the whole project (root + every subagent); `build` fails if two agents share a name.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `model`                                                                                                                                                            | string           | A `provider/model` slug or a bare provider name. A `profile` (see [Models and profiles](/conventions/models/index.html)) can stand in for it. See below.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `description`                                                                                                                                                      | string           | Optional.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `subAgents`                                                                                                                                                        | array of strings | Names of sibling folders under the root project's `subagents/`. See [subagents/](/conventions/subagents/index.html).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `mcpServers`                                                                                                                                                       | array            | MCP servers - each entry a URL string, or a mapping with `url` (or `command`), `name` and the credentials the server wants. See [mcp/](/conventions/mcp/index.html).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `security`                                                                                                                                                         | struct           | Forwarded verbatim into the generated app's `bxai` module settings; bx-ai's own `SecurityDirector` turns it into guardrail middleware. Passthrough only - BxAgents has no own guardrails convention.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `memory`                                                                                                                                                           | string or struct | The agent's conversation memory. A bare string is shorthand for the type (`"cache"`); a struct is `{ type, ...config }` and is passed through to `aiMemory()` verbatim - e.g. `{ type: "cache", maxMessages: 50 }`, or with `summaryProvider`/`summaryModel`/`summaryThreshold` to make the web UI's `/compact` functional. Applies per node, so a subagent can declare its own.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `checkpointer`                                                                                                                                                     | struct           | `{ type: "cache"\|"file"\|"jdbc", ...config }`. Defaults to `{ type: "cache" }` if omitted. Always applied - without one, human-in-the-loop approval flows through any gateway other than `cli` fail outright.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `gatewaySession`                                                                                                                                                   | struct           | `{ policy, maxQueueDepth, attachments, commands }`, all optional (default `"queue"` / `50` / `true` / a safe set of [slash commands](/conventions/gateways/index.html#commands-in-a-gateway)). Only meaningful if the project has at least one push-style [gateway](/conventions/gateways/index.html#3-push-style-gateways-type-telegram--slack--discord--email--whatsapp-cloud--teams--twilio--github--signal-and-friends) entry - controls the generated `GatewaySession`'s policy for a second inbound message arriving on a thread that already has a turn in flight. `policy` must be one of `reject`/`queue`/`steer`/`interrupt`. |
| `agentApi`                                                                                                                                                         | struct           | `{ enabled, access, tokenEnvVar, tokens, profiles, path, allowedIPs, rateLimit, manageTokens }`, all optional. Controls the always-on agent route, at `/__bxagents` unless `path` moves it. See [The always-on agent route](#the-always-on-agent-route) below.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `tools`, `toolOptions`                                                                                                                                             | array, struct    | Module tools and their options. See [Tools](/conventions/agent-yaml/index.html#tools) and [Tool options](/conventions/agent-yaml/index.html#tool-options).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `provider`, `params`, `options`, `providers`, `profiles`, `defaultProfile`, `profile`, `contextWindow`, `vision`, `embeddings`, `speech`, `transcription`, `image` | various          | The model settings, with the same shape and checks as in [`Agent.yaml`](/conventions/agent-yaml/index.html). A subagent may not set `params`, `options`, `providers`, `profiles`, `defaultProfile` or the four capabilities: they apply to the whole app and belong to the root. See [Models and profiles](/conventions/models/index.html).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `notes`                                                                                                                                                            | struct           | Short notes the agent keeps. See [Notes](/conventions/agent-yaml/index.html#notes).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `usage`                                                                                                                                                            | boolean          | Records what each model call used. Root only. See [`usage`](/conventions/agent-yaml/index.html#settings).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `tui`                                                                                                                                                              | struct           | How the terminal chat looks. Root only. See [`tui`](/conventions/agent-yaml/index.html#settings).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `extensions`                                                                                                                                                       | struct           | Values for the project's [extensions](/conventions/extensions/index.html). Root only.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| any other key                                                                                                                                                      | any              | Merged and available in the resolved config struct, but not interpreted by BxAgents itself.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |

## The model slug

`model` is BxAgents' own convention - bx-ai itself takes `provider` and `model` as two separate arguments to `aiModel()`. BxAgents splits the slug **on the first `/` only** , so a provider that itself contains a slash (like OpenRouter's `openrouter/anthropic/claude-x`) still parses correctly:

|          `model` value          |   provider   |        model         |
|---------------------------------|--------------|----------------------|
| `openai/gpt-5`                  | `openai`     | `gpt-5`              |
| `openrouter/anthropic/claude-x` | `openrouter` | `anthropic/claude-x` |
| `mock/mock-model`               | `mock`       | `mock-model`         |

If `model` has no `/` at all, it must be a known core provider name (the provider's default model) - validation rejects anything else. The recognized core providers are: `bedrock`, `cartesia`, `claude`, `cloudflare`, `cohere`, `deepseek`, `docker`, `elevenlabs`, `gemini`, `grok`, `groq`, `huggingface`, `minimax`, `mistral`, `mock`, `ollama`, `openai`, `openai-compatible`, `openrouter`, `perplexity`, `voyage` (kept in sync with bx-ai's own `CORE_PROVIDERS`). `mock` is a real provider, useful for tests and CI - it never makes a network call.

This slug-splitting convention is what a `configure()`-declared `model` string goes through - `super.init()`'s own `model` argument instead takes a real `AiModel` instance directly (`aiModel( provider: "...", params: { model: "..." } )`), since the class already speaks bx-ai's own API.

## Environment overrides

`Agent.bx` may declare a method named after an environment (e.g. `production()`, `development()`, or any custom name) returning a struct of overrides - this works whether or not the class also declares a `configure()`:

```javascript
class extends="bxModules.bxai.models.runnables.AiAgent" {

	function init() {
		super.init(
			name        : "override-agent",
			description : "An agent with an environment override",
			model       : aiModel( provider: "openai", params: { model: "gpt-5" } )
		)
		return this
	}

	function production() {
		return {
			model : "openai/gpt-5-mini"
		};
	}

}
```

The active environment is resolved with this precedence (highest wins):

1. `--environment` CLI flag (`bxAgents build --environment=production`)
2. `Agent.bx`'s own `detectEnvironment()` method, if it declares one
3. `BX_AGENTS_ENV` environment variable
4. `"development"` (default)

### `detectEnvironment()`

For anything the first and third tiers can't express, `Agent.bx` may declare a
`detectEnvironment()` method and decide for itself. Whatever it returns is taken
as the environment name verbatim:

```javascript
class extends="bxModules.bxai.models.runnables.AiAgent" {

	function init() {
		super.init( name : "my-agent", model : aiModel( provider : "openai", params : { model : "gpt-5" } ) )
		return this
	}

	function detectEnvironment() {
		return fileExists( expandPath( "/.production-marker" ) ) ? "production" : "development";
	}

}
```

This mirrors ColdBox's own tier-1 convention (a config declaring
`detectEnvironment()` has its return value taken verbatim), with two deliberate
differences, both because this runs at **build** time:

* An explicit `--environment` flag **outranks** `detectEnvironment()` here, where ColdBox puts its own detect method first. A flag someone typed is the most specific statement of intent available.
* ColdBox's *other* detection tier - an `environments` struct of regexes matched against `CGI.HTTP_HOST` - is **not** supported. It cannot work here: the build runs in a CLI process with no HTTP host, so it would only ever describe the machine doing the building (a CI runner would resolve `development` for a production build).

Returning a blank string, or anything that isn't a string, means "no opinion" and
falls through to the next tier - so a project computing its environment from
something absent on this machine degrades to the default rather than failing the
build. A `detectEnvironment()` that **throws** is a different matter: that's a real
bug in the project's own code, and `build` fails and says so.

This is a **build-time** decision only, distinct from ColdBox's own runtime environment detection (the generated app reads `getSetting("environment")` on its own, per ColdBox's `environments` convention) - this precedence only decides which `environment()` override method on `Agent.bx`, and which `boxlang-{env}.json`/`miniserver-{env}.json` files, the build pipeline applies.

If no method matching the active environment exists, no override is applied.

## Merge semantics

The full resolution order (lowest to highest precedence) is:

1. `configure()` (optional)
2. the matching environment-override method, if any
3. `boxlang.json`
4. `boxlang-{environment}.json`
5. `miniserver.json`
6. `miniserver-{environment}.json`

Struct keys are merged **recursively** - a nested struct in a higher-precedence source only overrides the keys it actually sets, leaving sibling keys from a lower-precedence source intact. Arrays and all scalar values are **replaced whole**, never appended or concatenated.

`boxlang.json`/`boxlang-{env}.json`/`miniserver.json`/`miniserver-{env}.json` are all optional project-root JSON files, useful for config that's easier to express as data than as BoxLang code (e.g. model defaults):

```json
// boxlang.json
{
	"modelDefaults": { "temperature": 0.7, "maxTokens": 1000 }
}
```

```json
// boxlang-production.json
{
	"modelDefaults": { "temperature": 0.2 }
}
```

Building with `--environment=production` here yields `modelDefaults: { temperature: 0.2, maxTokens: 1000 }` - the recursive merge kept `maxTokens` from the base file since `boxlang-production.json` never mentioned it.
> **Warning**
>
> Secrets (API keys, tokens) are never read or merged by BxAgents at build time - they stay external (an OS environment variable, `.env`, a platform secret manager) and are resolved live by bx-ai itself at runtime. See [Deployment \& Secrets](/deployment-and-secrets/index.html).

## The always-on agent route

Every built project exposes its root agent over HTTP at a fixed reserved path,
whether or not it declares any [`gateways/`](/conventions/gateways/index.html) entries:

    POST /__bxagents/invoke
    POST /__bxagents/stream    # SSE
    POST /__bxagents/batch
    GET  /__bxagents/info

They answer in the shape ColdBox's `toAi()` terminator gives, but they are routes of the agent API's own handler,
so the same [access setting](#agentapi) covers them and every other route. (ColdBox route middleware does not
reach `toAi()`'s routes, which is why they are not used.) The
route exists so this module's own tooling always has an address to talk to -
it's the service entrance, not your project's public API. A project's own
public surface belongs in `gateways/`, at whatever paths you choose.

A route reached with a verb it does not take (a `GET` to `/invoke`) answers `405` with the usual JSON body, `{ "success": false, "error": "...", "code": "method_not_allowed" }`, not an error page.

### Run control

Beside those four, a generated handler (`handlers/AgentApi.bx`) serves what a chat client needs to
control a run. It is what `chat --server` and `chat --connect` use:

    POST /__bxagents/events    # SSE: like /stream, plus tool and suspended frames. Body may carry
                               # attachments: [ { name, mime, data (base64) } ], at most 4 pictures of 5 MB
    POST /__bxagents/cancel    # { threadId, reason? }
    POST /__bxagents/steer     # { threadId, input }
    GET  /__bxagents/pending   # ?threadId=
    POST /__bxagents/resume    # { threadId, decision } -> SSE, like /events
    GET  /__bxagents/tools
    GET  /__bxagents/profiles   # the profiles a client may ask for
    GET  /__bxagents/agent    # name, model, what it can do
    GET  /__bxagents/sessions   # the caller's recent conversations (?source=terminal for those that started there; ?all=1 lists everyone's, with whose each is, for an admin)
    POST /__bxagents/sessions   # { title? } start one: { conversationId }
    POST /__bxagents/sessions/rename   # { conversationId, title } name one
    POST /__bxagents/sessions/fork     # { conversationId, title? } copy one, messages and all
    POST /__bxagents/sessions/delete   # { conversationId } its row and the agent's messages for it
    GET  /__bxagents/export    # ?conversationId=&format=md|html the conversation as a file to save
    GET  /__bxagents/whoami    # who the server takes the caller to be: { id, name, scope, source, agent }
    GET  /__bxagents/volumes   # the folders the agent may use: { volumes: [ { name, mode, description } ] }, never a path on the machine
    GET  /__bxagents/logs      # the agent's logs, admin only: which there are, or ?area=&tail=&level=&q= for the last lines
    GET  /__bxagents/gateways  # the chat apps and their state, admin only: { gateways: [ { name, type, state, credentials, lastActiveAt, lastError } ] }
    GET  /__bxagents/skills    # the skills the agent can load: { skills: [ { name, description, origin } ] }, origin is installed, project or agent
    GET  /__bxagents/data      # where the agent keeps everything and where each volume is (admin only)
    GET  /__bxagents/users     # the sign-in accounts and whether each is an admin (admin only)
    POST /__bxagents/users/admin  # { username, admin }: make an account an admin or take that away (admin only)
    GET  /__bxagents/preferences          # what the caller has set: { preferences : { key : value } }
    POST /__bxagents/preferences/set      # { key, value }
    POST /__bxagents/preferences/delete   # { key }
    GET  /__bxagents/history    # ?conversationId= what was said in one
    POST /__bxagents/clear      # { conversationId } forget its messages
    POST /__bxagents/compact    # { conversationId } summarize the older messages
    POST /__bxagents/ping       # { profile? } test a model with one tiny question: { ok, model, ms, reply } or { ok : false, model, reason }
    GET  /__bxagents/commands   # the slash commands this caller may run, [ { name, hint } ]
    GET  /__bxagents/context    # ?conversationId= estimated size of the context: parts, largest tools, total, share of the window
    GET  /__bxagents/status     # ?conversationId= what the extensions' status items say: { items : [ { name, text } ] }
    GET  /__bxagents/slots      # ?conversationId= what the extensions' slots hold: { items : [ { id, extension, place, html, text } ] }
    POST /__bxagents/command    # { line : "/info", conversationId? } run one, answers { blocks, effects, conversationId }
    GET  /__bxagents/notes    # the caller's notes and the agent's, with how full they are
    POST /__bxagents/notes    # { scope : "user" | "agent", text }
    POST /__bxagents/notes/update   # { scope, id, text }
    POST /__bxagents/notes/remove   # { scope, id }

`/events` sends the frames of `/stream` (`thread` first, `chunk` for each piece of the answer, `done` last)
and adds:

|    Frame    |                                                      Data                                                      |
|-------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `tool`      | `{ id, name, arguments, status, ms }`, once with `status: "running"` and once with `"ok"` and the time it took |
| `suspended` | `{ threadId, pendingActions : [ { toolName, toolArgs } ] }` when the run waits for a human decision            |
| `error`     | `{ message }`                                                                                                  |

`cancel` stops the run at its next checkpoint (before the next model call or tool call, not in the middle of
a token). `steer` splices a message into a run in flight. `resume` takes `approve`, `approve_session` or
`reject` and streams the rest of the turn. A run belongs to whoever started it: `pending` answers "nothing
pending" and `resume` answers `403` to anyone else.

Send a `conversationId` with `/events` to keep the turn in a conversation: the server lists it under the caller (the name of the token used, or `local` on an open route) and the agent's memory keeps its messages under the same id. `sessions`, `history`, `clear` and `compact` work on the caller's own conversations only; someone else's id is a `404`, the same as one that does not exist. They answer `404` when the server has no shared chat database, and `compact` reports `available: false` when the agent's memory has no summary model.

The `notes` routes answer `404` for an agent that has no [`notes`](/conventions/agent-yaml/index.html#notes) block. Each caller reads and changes their own user notes (the owner is the name of the token they used, or `local` on an open route) and the agent's notes. Any caller can add to either scope or edit a note; removing a note of the agent needs an `admin` token (a `403` otherwise), because it changes what every user's agent knows.

These routes sit behind the same `x-bxagents-token` gate as the other four (a missing or wrong token is a
`401`), and `agentApi.enabled: false` removes all of them.

### Answers, errors and who is calling

Every answer is JSON with `success`. A failure is `{ "success": false, "error": "text for people", "code": "machine_code" }` with the status the code means:

| Status |                     Codes                      |
|--------|------------------------------------------------|
| 400    | `bad_request`, `bad_profile`, `bad_attachment` |
| 401    | `unauthorized`                                 |
| 403    | `forbidden`, `csrf`, `not_your_run`            |
| 404    | `not_found`, `no_notes`                        |
| 409    | `busy`, `conflict`                             |
| 429    | `rate_limited`                                 |
| 500    | `internal`                                     |

On a route that is open, everyone is the one user `local`, on every surface, so the terminal chat, the web page and a script share conversations and notes. A caller can say which surface it is with the `x-bxagents-source` header (`web`, `terminal`, or any plain lower case name; `api` when it sends none). The conversation list records it: `GET /__bxagents/sessions` returns a `source` for each conversation, and `?source=terminal` lists only those. Conversations that were made before this was recorded have a blank source.

Because the path is reserved, `build` **rejects** any `gateways/` entry whose
`path` is `/__bxagents` or sits underneath it. Two routes on one mount is a
genuine conflict: one would silently shadow the other, and yours would be the
one that never answers.

### `agentApi`

`configure()` may return an `agentApi` struct to control it:

|      Key       |       Type        |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
|----------------|-------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `enabled`      | boolean           | Default `true`. Set `false` to omit the route entirely - for a build going somewhere it has no business existing.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `access`       | `open` or `token` | Whether callers must prove who they are. Left out, it follows the next two keys: a `tokenEnvVar` or `tokens: true` means `token`, nothing means `open`. `open` with either of those set, or `token` with neither, is a build error.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `tokenEnvVar`  | string            | The **name** of an environment variable holding a shared secret. When set, every route requires a matching `x-bxagents-token` request header.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `tokens`       | boolean           | Default `false`. `true` also accepts the [access tokens](#access-tokens-for-a-deployed-agent) made with `bxAgents token create`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `path`         | string            | Default `/__bxagents`. Where the whole API is served, e.g. `/agent-api`: a rooted path of plain segments (letters, digits, `_`, `-`, `~`). Everything on this page that says `/__bxagents` means this path. A `gateways/` entry may not sit on it. The web page, `serve` and `chat --server` follow it by themselves; `chat --connect` to a server that moved it needs `--api-path=/agent-api`.                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `allowedIPs`   | list              | Default none (anyone). The addresses and networks that may call at all, e.g. `[ "10.0.0.0/8", "203.0.113.7", "::1" ]`. It is cbSecurity's own `AllowedIPs` route middleware in front of every route, so anyone else gets `403` (`{ "error": true, "messages": [ "Your IP address is not allowed" ] }`) before any token is looked at. It checks the address of the connection, never a `X-Forwarded-For` header the client chooses; behind a reverse proxy every caller has the proxy's address unless you set cbSecurity's `middleware.trustedProxies`. `/health` stays open. |
| `rateLimit`    | struct            | Default none. `{ requests, perSeconds }`: at most `requests` calls from one address in each window of `perSeconds` seconds. It is cbSecurity's own `Throttle` route middleware, one counter for the whole API, kept in CacheBox. Over the limit answers `429` with a `Retry-After` header; every answer carries `X-RateLimit-Limit` and `X-RateLimit-Remaining`.                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `manageTokens` | boolean           | Default `false`. `true` lets an admin make, list and revoke [access tokens](#access-tokens-for-a-deployed-agent) over the API (`GET`/`POST /__bxagents/tokens`, `POST /__bxagents/tokens/revoke`) and shows a **Tokens** panel in the web page. Needs `tokens: true` and a token API; a `chat` token gets `403`. The secret of a new token is in the answer to the create call and nowhere else. Off, the routes do not exist and tokens are made only with `bxAgents token create`.                                                                                           |
| `profiles`     | list              | Default none. The [profiles](/conventions/models/index.html#profiles) a client may ask for with `options.profile` on `/events`, and what `GET /__bxagents/profiles` lists (never a key). Any other profile is a `400`, so a caller cannot pick a model you did not offer. `chat --connect` uses this list for `/profile`. Each name must be declared in `Agent.yaml`, or `default`.                                                                                                                                                                                            |

```javascript
function configure() {
	return {
		name     : "my-agent",
		model    : "openai/gpt-5",
		agentApi : {
			tokenEnvVar : "BXAGENTS_API_TOKEN"
		}
	};
}
```

Because this comes from `configure()`, it scopes per environment with an
[environment override](#environment-overrides) like any other key - so a
project can leave the route open locally and require a token in production:

```javascript
function production() {
	return {
		agentApi : { tokenEnvVar : "BXAGENTS_API_TOKEN" }
	};
}
```

### Who may stop a run

`POST /cancel` and `POST /steer` take a `threadId`, which is not a secret (the first frame of every stream carries it). A run can only be stopped or steered by the caller who started it: anyone else gets `403` with `code: "not_your_run"`. A run no caller here started (one a chat platform's gateway runs) can only be touched by an `admin`; anyone else is told `cancelled: false`, the same answer an unknown thread id gets.

### Open or token

`access: open` (the default when nothing else is set) asks nobody anything: everyone is the one `local` user. It is meant for your own machine. When `serve` is told to listen on an address other machines can reach (`--host=0.0.0.0`, say) and the API is open, it prints a warning at start:

    WARNING: the agent API is open and this server listens on every network interface (port 8080). Anyone who can reach it can chat with the agent, use its tools and read its conversations. Set agentApi.access to token ...

`access: token` puts every route of the API behind one check, made before any action runs, by ColdBox route middleware. That includes `invoke`, `stream`, `batch` and `info`, and the same four routes of any [gateway that exposes the agent](/conventions/gateways/index.html) (`exposes: "agent"`), which follow this one switch. A request that carries neither the shared secret nor an issued token is answered `401` and never reaches the agent.

The gate **fails closed** : if the named variable is unset or blank at runtime,
nothing matches - it never degenerates into comparing `""` to `""` and letting
every caller through. A request without a valid token gets a `401` with a small
JSON body (`code: unauthorized`), and never reaches the agent.
> **Warning**
>
> `tokenEnvVar` names a **variable** , never the secret itself. `build` rejects
> a value that isn't a valid environment-variable name, precisely so a literal
> token can't be committed here by mistake. Only the variable's name is ever
> written into generated source.

### Access tokens for a deployed agent

One shared secret (`tokenEnvVar`) is enough for a single caller. To let several people or machines in, each with a name you can revoke, turn on issued tokens:

```yaml
# Agent.yaml
agentApi:
  tokens: true
```

Make them where the agent's database is: on the server, or in the project before you pack it.

```bash
bxAgents token create --name=laptop --expires=90d
bxAgents token create --name=ci --scope=admin
bxAgents token list
bxAgents token revoke --name=laptop
```

* A token is shown **once**, when it is made. Only its SHA-256 is stored, so a stolen database file cannot be used to call the agent.
* The caller sends it in the `x-bxagents-token` header, or `bxAgents chat --connect=<url> --token=<token>` (or `BXAGENTS_TOKEN`) does.
* The name is who is calling. A run belongs to the token that started it, and one token cannot answer another's pending approval. The scope is `chat` or `admin`.
* Revoking takes effect on the next request, without a restart. A token can also expire (`--expires=90d`, `12h`, `2w` or a date).
* With `tokens: true` and no `tokenEnvVar`, a server with no tokens yet refuses everyone. With both, the shared secret works as an `admin` token, so a fresh deployment can be reached before the first token exists.
* The tokens live in the [shared chat database](/conventions/web-ui/index.html#the-sqlite-store) (`data/chat.db`). On a deployed server run `token` with `BXAGENTS_DB` pointing at the file the app uses.

Put HTTPS in front of any server a token travels to: a token on plain HTTP can be read on the wire.
> **Info**
>
> The route is bound to whatever host the [miniserver](/cli-reference/index.html#serve)
> is listening on - `127.0.0.1` by default, so nothing is reachable off the
> machine unless you deliberately expose it. `tokenEnvVar` is what matters once
> you do, and for any built `.bxa` artifact you deploy.

title: Agent.yaml
body: Agent.yaml Agent.yaml is the default way to define an agent. It is a plain YAML file - a name, a model, and any of the optional settings below - and the build turns it into a running agent. Most agents need nothing more than this file and an instructions.md beside it. name: support description: Answers customer questions about orders model: openai/gpt-5 environments: test: model: mock/mock-model bxAgents new scaffolds exactly this shape. When the definition needs real code (hooks, dynamic instructions, tools registered in code), use the advanced option instead: a class-based Agent.bx , scaffolded with bxAgents new --class . Info A folder holds one agent definition. An Agent.yaml (or Agent.yml ) together with an Agent.bx in the same folder is an error - two definitions of one agent would leave it ambiguous which settings win - and build fails and names both files so you can keep one. This applies to the project root and to every subagent folder, and a project can mix the two: a YAML root with a class-based subagent, or the other way round. Settings Key Type Notes name string Also becomes this agent's config/WireBox.bx binding key at build time, so it must be unique across the whole project (root + every subagent). model string A provider/model slug, a bare provider name, or a model name when provider is set. See The model slug and Models and profiles . provider string The default provider, a bx-ai provider name. With model as a bare model name. See Models and profiles . params mapping Default request parameters, such as temperature . options mapping Default provider options, such as timeout . providers mapping Per provider params and options , by provider name. profiles mapping Named combinations. Each profile takes description , provider , model , params , options , apiKeyEnv (the name of the variable that holds the key, never the key) and optionally contextWindow and vision . See Models and profiles . contextWindow , vision number, boolean What the default model can hold (tokens) and whether it can see images. Optional facts for the chat; bx-ai does not read them. See Models . defaultProfile string The profile used when nothing asks for another. profile string The profile this agent uses. embeddings , speech , transcription , image mapping bx-ai's capability defaults: provider , model and a few settings each. description string Optional. instructions string Optional inline instructions. See Instructions . tools list of strings Module tools this agent gets, as item@module or *@module . See Tools . toolOptions mapping Options for a module's tools, keyed by module name. See Tool options . subAgents list of strings Names of sibling folders under the root project's subagents/ . See subagents/ . mcpServers list MCP servers - each entry a URL string, a mapping with url and the credentials the server wants ( token , headers , timeout ), or a mapping with command for a server that runs as a program ( env , cwd , prefix , toolFilter ). See mcp/ . A web server can take oauth so each person signs in to it: see connect . security mapping Forwarded verbatim into the generated app's bxai module settings; bx-ai's own SecurityDirector turns it into guardrail middleware. memory string or mapping The agent's conversation memory. A memory is keyed by the agent's name, so one that is kept on disk is found again on the next start; set key in the mapping to name it yourself. checkpointer mapping { type: cache\|file\|jdbc, ...config } . Defaults to { type: cache } if omitted. gatewaySession mapping { policy, maxQueueDepth, attachments, commands } , all optional. policy is queue (default), reject , steer or interrupt . attachments: false switches off pictures and files sent in chat apps. commands is { enabled, prefix, prefixes, conversation, allow, admins } . See Notes . vault mapping Gives the agent vault_list and vault_request and scrubs vault secrets from tool results. vault: {} turns it on. See the vault . routines mapping Prompts the agent runs on a schedule, made by asking it. Off unless enabled: true . maxPerUser , minInterval , maxParallel , maxPromptLength , approvalTimeout , timezone , summaryLength , maxReportSize and maxReportFiles set the limits. See routines . skills mapping Skills the agent saves for itself. agentCanSave (default true ) gives the root agent a skill_save tool; autoApprove (default false ) skips the person's approval of each save. Saved skills live in the data home and are in the agent's skill list at once. See data and volumes . data mapping Where the agent keeps everything: data: { home: ~/.nanobox } . See data and volumes . Only in the project's own Agent.yaml . volumes mapping Host folders the agent's file tools may use, by name: volumes: { notes: { path: ~/Notes, mode: rw } } . See data and volumes . Only in the project's own Agent.yaml . usage boolean Records what each model call used (the time, who, the provider, the model and the tokens), for bxAgents stats and /stats . Off by default : set usage: true to turn it on. Counts only, never what was said. Only in the project's own Agent.yaml . Rebuild after changing it. tui mapping How the terminal chat looks: { prompt, widgets: { top, bottom } } , all optional. prompt is bars (default), bars-hints , rule , box or panel ; widgets list what goes in the top bar and at the bottom ( agent , profile , folder , user , clock , machine , git , date , session , elapsed , ctx ). See The prompt and the tables . extensions mapping Values for the project's extensions , by extension name, and what to turn off: { disable: [ roll, "deploy:deploy" ], deploy: { target: production } } . Each extension's block is merged over the defaults its configure() sets. Only in the project's own Agent.yaml . environments mapping Per-environment overrides. See Environments . These are the same settings an Agent.bx 's configure() returns, so every behavior documented for them applies unchanged. Warning An unknown key is an error , and the message lists the valid ones. A typo such as modle: would otherwise do nothing, quietly. Anything free-form belongs in an Agent.bx . A value of the wrong type (a text where a list belongs, say) and an empty value ( model: with nothing after it) are errors too. Any other value is the name of a class that implements INotesProvider and is created with ( config, agentName ) , for a notes service of your own. user.limit 1400 Characters of notes about the user, a whole number from 100 to 20000. Each user has their own. agent.limit 2200 Characters of notes about the agent's work, a whole number from 100 to 20000. Shared by everyone who talks to it. tool true remember (save or replace a note) and forget (remove one). Without them the notes are read-only for the agent and a person manages them. approveForget true A run that wants to forget stops for approval , like any tool that needs it. Saving a note needs none. How it works: Both scopes go into the system prompt as short lists, oldest first, within their limits. They are read once per conversation, so the prompt stays the same turn to turn (a provider's prompt cache keeps working) and a note saved now shows from the next conversation. A note is one line of at most 500 characters. Nothing is dropped silently: a note that does not fit the limit is refused, and the agent is told how full the notes are so it can replace or forget an older one. The agent scope belongs to the agent's name . The terminal chat, the web chat and the server share one file, data/chat.db (see the SQLite store ). Manage them yourself with /remember and /notes in chat , with bxAgents notes from a shell, or over HTTP through the run-control routes . Instructions The agent's instructions are its system prompt. Put them in an instructions.md beside Agent.yaml , the usual choice because the file is plain Markdown and easy to edit: my-agent/ ├── Agent.yaml └── instructions.md For a short prompt you can write them inline instead: name: greeter model: openai/gpt-5 instructions: | You greet people by name. Keep it to one sentence. If both exist, instructions.md wins - the file is the more deliberate choice, so a stray instructions: line cannot override it. If neither exists, build fails and says so. Environments environments holds overrides keyed by environment name. It is the YAML spelling of the environment-override methods ( production() ) an Agent.bx can declare: name: support model: openai/gpt-5 environments: production: model: openai/gpt-5-mini staging: description: Staging copy The active environment is chosen with this precedence, highest first: the --environment CLI flag ( bxAgents build --environment=production ) the BX_AGENTS_ENV environment variable development Only the block for the active environment is applied, on top of the top-level settings; keys it does not mention are left alone. Each block accepts the same keys as the top level, except environments itself. bxAgents test builds against the test environment, which is why a scaffolded project carries a test block pointing at the mock provider: its tests need no API key or network access. Note An Agent.yaml cannot compute its environment. The detectEnvironment() method described under Environment overrides needs code, so a project that needs it uses an Agent.bx . The overrides then merge with boxlang.json , boxlang-{environment}.json , miniserver.json and miniserver-{environment}.json exactly as described in Merge semantics . Requirements Reading YAML needs the bx-yaml module, 1.1.0 or later . BxAgents bundles it, so there is nothing to install. Global YAML tags (such as !!java.io.File ) are rejected, so a cloned project's Agent.yaml cannot make the build instantiate arbitrary Java classes. YAML or Agent.bx? Use When Agent.yaml The agent is configuration: a name, a model, instructions, memory, subagents. This is almost every agent. Agent.bx The definition itself needs code: hooks, dynamic instructions, tools registered in code, an overridden method, or detectEnvironment() . You can start with YAML and switch later: create the Agent.bx , move the settings across, and delete the Agent.yaml .

# Agent.yaml

`Agent.yaml` is the default way to define an agent. It is a plain YAML file - a name, a model, and any of the optional settings below - and the build turns it into a running agent. Most agents need nothing more than this file and an [`instructions.md`](#instructions) beside it.

```yaml
name: support
description: Answers customer questions about orders
model: openai/gpt-5

environments:
  test:
    model: mock/mock-model
```

`bxAgents new` scaffolds exactly this shape. When the definition needs real code (hooks, dynamic instructions, tools registered in code), use the advanced option instead: a class-based [`Agent.bx`](/conventions/agent-bx/index.html), scaffolded with `bxAgents new --class`.
> **Info**
>
> A folder holds **one** agent definition. An `Agent.yaml` (or `Agent.yml`) together with an `Agent.bx` in the same folder is an error - two definitions of one agent would leave it ambiguous which settings win - and `build` fails and names both files so you can keep one. This applies to the project root and to every [subagent](/conventions/subagents/index.html) folder, and a project can mix the two: a YAML root with a class-based subagent, or the other way round.

## Settings

|                       Key                        |       Type        |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
|--------------------------------------------------|-------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `name`                                           | string            | Also becomes this agent's `config/WireBox.bx` binding key at build time, so it must be unique across the whole project (root + every subagent).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `model`                                          | string            | A `provider/model` slug, a bare provider name, or a model name when `provider` is set. See [The model slug](/conventions/agent-bx/index.html#the-model-slug) and [Models and profiles](/conventions/models/index.html).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `provider`                                       | string            | The default provider, a bx-ai provider name. With `model` as a bare model name. See [Models and profiles](/conventions/models/index.html).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `params`                                         | mapping           | Default request parameters, such as `temperature`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `options`                                        | mapping           | Default provider options, such as `timeout`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `providers`                                      | mapping           | Per provider `params` and `options`, by provider name.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `profiles`                                       | mapping           | Named combinations. Each profile takes `description`, `provider`, `model`, `params`, `options`, `apiKeyEnv` (the name of the variable that holds the key, never the key) and optionally `contextWindow` and `vision`. See [Models and profiles](/conventions/models/index.html#profiles).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `contextWindow`, `vision`                        | number, boolean   | What the default model can hold (tokens) and whether it can see images. Optional facts for the chat; bx-ai does not read them. See [Models](/conventions/models/index.html#what-the-project-knows-about-a-model).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
