| `embeddings`, `speech`, `transcription`, `image` | mapping           | bx-ai's capability defaults: `provider`, `model` and a few settings each.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `description`                                    | string            | Optional.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `instructions`                                   | string            | Optional inline instructions. See [Instructions](#instructions).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `tools`                                          | list of strings   | Module tools this agent gets, as `item@module` or `*@module`. See [Tools](#tools).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `toolOptions`                                    | mapping           | Options for a module's tools, keyed by module name. See [Tool options](#tool-options).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `subAgents`                                      | list of strings   | Names of sibling folders under the root project's `subagents/`. See [subagents/](/conventions/subagents/index.html).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `mcpServers`                                     | list              | MCP servers - each entry a URL string, a mapping with `url` and the credentials the server wants (`token`, `headers`, `timeout`), or a mapping with `command` for a server that runs as a program (`env`, `cwd`, `prefix`, `toolFilter`). See [mcp/](/conventions/mcp/index.html). A web server can take `oauth` so each person signs in to it: see [connect](/conventions/connect/index.html).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `security`                                       | mapping           | Forwarded verbatim into the generated app's `bxai` module settings; bx-ai's own `SecurityDirector` turns it into guardrail middleware.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `memory`                                         | string or mapping | The agent's conversation memory. Left out, every agent (the root and each subagent) remembers in the chat database, one row per person and conversation under its own name, so the same person finds the same conversation from the terminal, the web page and the API. `maxMessages` (20 to 100000, default 500) is the most it keeps of one conversation, dropping the oldest, and `keepRecent` (default 20, lower than `maxMessages`) is how many of the latest messages stay as they are when `/compact` summarizes the rest. A bare string is a memory type (`cache`); a mapping with a `type` is `{ type, ...config }` passed through to `aiMemory()` exactly as written, and replaces the default. A memory is keyed by the agent's name, so one that is kept on disk is found again on the next start; set `key` in the mapping to name it yourself. |
| `checkpointer`                                   | mapping           | `{ type: cache\|file\|jdbc, ...config }`. Defaults to `{ type: cache }` if omitted.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `gatewaySession`                                 | mapping           | `{ policy, maxQueueDepth, attachments, commands }`, all optional. `policy` is `queue` (default), `reject`, `steer` or `interrupt`. `attachments: false` switches off pictures and files sent in chat apps. `commands` is `{ enabled, prefix, prefixes, conversation, allow, admins }`. See [Gateways](/conventions/gateways/index.html#commands-in-a-gateway).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `agentApi`                                       | mapping           | `{ enabled, access, tokenEnvVar, tokens, profiles, path, allowedIPs, rateLimit, manageTokens }`, all optional. `enabled` defaults to `true`, `access` to `open` (or `token` when `tokenEnvVar` or `tokens` is set), `tokens` and `manageTokens` to `false`, `path` to `/__bxagents`. See [`agentApi`](/conventions/agent-bx/index.html#agentapi) for each key.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `notes`                                          | mapping           | Short notes the agent keeps about the user and its own work. `notes: {}` turns them on with the defaults. See [Notes](#notes).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `vault`                                          | mapping           | Gives the agent `vault_list` and `vault_request` and scrubs vault secrets from tool results. `vault: {}` turns it on. See [the vault](/conventions/vault/index.html).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `routines`                                       | mapping           | Prompts the agent runs on a schedule, made by asking it. Off unless `enabled: true`. `maxPerUser`, `minInterval`, `maxParallel`, `maxPromptLength`, `approvalTimeout`, `timezone`, `summaryLength`, `maxReportSize` and `maxReportFiles` set the limits. See [routines](/conventions/routines/index.html).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `skills`                                         | mapping           | Skills the agent saves for itself. `agentCanSave` (default `true`) gives the root agent a `skill_save` tool; `autoApprove` (default `false`) skips the person's approval of each save. Saved skills live in the data home and are in the agent's skill list at once. See [data and volumes](/conventions/data/index.html#skills-the-agent-saves).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `data`                                           | mapping           | Where the agent keeps everything: `data: { home: ~/.nanobox }`. See [data and volumes](/conventions/data/index.html). Only in the project's own `Agent.yaml`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `volumes`                                        | mapping           | Host folders the agent's file tools may use, by name: `volumes: { notes: { path: ~/Notes, mode: rw } }`. See [data and volumes](/conventions/data/index.html#volumes). Only in the project's own `Agent.yaml`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `usage`                                          | boolean           | Records what each model call used (the time, who, the provider, the model and the tokens), for [`bxAgents stats`](/cli-reference/index.html#stats) and `/stats`. **Off by default** : set `usage: true` to turn it on. Counts only, never what was said. Only in the project's own `Agent.yaml`. Rebuild after changing it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `tui`                                            | mapping           | How the terminal chat looks: `{ prompt, widgets: { top, bottom } }`, all optional. `prompt` is `bars` (default), `bars-hints`, `rule`, `box` or `panel`; `widgets` list what goes in the top bar and at the bottom (`agent`, `profile`, `folder`, `user`, `clock`, `machine`, `git`, `date`, `session`, `elapsed`, `ctx`). A wrong name is refused and the valid ones are listed. Only in the project's own `Agent.yaml`. See [The prompt and the tables](/cli-reference/index.html#the-prompt-and-the-tables).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |

Only in the project's own `Agent.yaml`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |

These are the same settings an `Agent.bx`'s `configure()` returns, so every behavior documented for them applies unchanged.
> **Warning**
>
> An **unknown key is an error** , and the message lists the valid ones. A typo such as `modle:` would otherwise do nothing, quietly. Anything free-form belongs in an `Agent.bx`.

A value of the wrong type (a text where a list belongs, say) and an empty value (`model:` with nothing after it) are errors too.

## Tools

An agent gets its own `tools/` folder, and nothing else, unless it asks. The tools other modules provide (bx-ai's built-ins, `bx-playwright`, ...) are a catalog: they are available, but an agent only has the ones its `tools:` list names. Every entry is `item@module`, the key bx-ai keeps them under:

```yaml
name: support
model: openai/gpt-5
tools:
  - now@bxai            # one tool from one module
  - "*@bxplaywright"    # every tool that module registered (quote it: * starts a YAML alias)
```

|          Entry           |         Gives the agent          |
|--------------------------|----------------------------------|
| `item@module`            | that one tool                    |
| `*@module`, or `@module` | every tool the module registered |

* **Default.** No `tools:` means only the agent's own `tools/`. This holds for every [subagent](/conventions/subagents/index.html) too: each one has its own `tools/` and its own `tools:`.
* **Naming a module validates it.** If the module is not installed, or has no such tool, `build` and the generated app fail with a message that lists what the module does provide.
* **A bare name is an error.** `now` fails with a hint to write `now@bxai`. bx-ai would otherwise resolve it to whichever module registered a tool called `now` first.
* **Own tools win.** If a tool in the agent's `tools/` has the same name as a module tool it selected, the own tool is used and the module tool is left out, with a warning in the `bxagents-tools` log.
* **Each tool once.** Listing a tool twice, or listing it along with a `*@module` that covers it, attaches it once.

### Tool options

`toolOptions` configures the tools of a module, keyed by **module name** . Two modules take options: `bxai`, for its [file tools](#file-tools), and `bxplaywright`, whose options are those of bx-playwright's `playwright()`: a `profile` (a name, or a list of names) and settings such as `headless`, `baseURL`, `browser`, `viewport` or `device`.

```yaml
tools:
  - "*@bxplaywright"
toolOptions:
  bxplaywright:
    profile: mobile
    headless: false
    baseURL: ${env.APP_URL:http://localhost:8080}
```

* **Each agent gets its own browser.** The browser tools bx-playwright registers share one browser for the whole app. An agent that lists `bxplaywright` tools does not get those: it gets a fresh set built for it alone (`playwright( profile, options ).aiTools()`), so a root agent and its subagent never drive the same page. The browser opens when one of its tools is first used, not at startup. `*@bxplaywright` works with no `toolOptions` at all and uses the module's own settings.
* **Environment values.** ``${env.NAME}` and `${env.NAME:default}`` are replaced with the environment variable when the app starts, never at build time, so a secret or a per-machine setting stays out of the project. A variable that is not set and has no default fails the agent at startup, naming it.
* **Checked at build time.** A key that is not a module the agent lists tools from, a module that takes no options, a key written as `item@module`, or an option bx-playwright does not have (the message lists the valid ones) is a `build` error.
* The module-wide settings (where browsers are installed, the default profile) stay in bx-playwright's own settings, not here.

### File tools

bx-ai has 19 file tools (`readFile`, `writeFile`, `listDirectory`, `searchFiles`, `deleteFile`, `zipFiles` and more), but it registers none of them. In BxAgents an agent gets them by listing them **and** naming the folders they may use in `toolOptions.bxai.allowedPaths`:

```yaml
tools:
  - readFile@bxai
  - listDirectory@bxai
toolOptions:
  bxai:
    allowedPaths:
      - tmp                  # the system temp folder
      - cwd                  # the folder the agent is started from
      - /data/reports        # or an absolute path
```

* **Each agent gets its own tools, locked to its own folders.** A path outside them is refused (`..` tricks included), and the tools are never put in the shared registry where another agent could pick them up.
* **No folders, no tools.** The tools exist only when `allowedPaths` is set, and an empty list is a build error, because bx-ai reads an empty list as "any path". Listing `readFile@bxai` with no `allowedPaths` fails with a message saying so.
* `now@bxai`, `httpGet@bxai`, `webSearch@bxai` and the rest of bx-ai's registered tools keep working as before, with or without `toolOptions.bxai`. `*@bxai` includes the file tools once `allowedPaths` is set.
* An entry may be `${env.NAME}` to take a folder from the environment.
* `bxAgents new` can write all of this for you: see [the new wizard](/guides/new-wizard/index.html).

## Notes

An agent can keep short notes: things about the user ("prefers short answers") and things about its own work ("the repo uses Gradle"). They are off until the block is there:

```yaml
notes: {}
```

```yaml
notes:
  provider: sqlite        # built in. Or a class implementing INotesProvider
  user:  { limit: 1400 }  # characters of user notes that go into the prompt
  agent: { limit: 2200 }  # characters of agent notes
  tool: true              # give the agent the note_remember and note_forget tools (default true)
  approveForget: true     # a person approves what the agent forgets (default true)
```

|       Key       | Default  |                                                                                                                                 Notes                                                                                                                                 |
|-----------------|----------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `provider`      | `sqlite` | `sqlite` keeps one row per note in the [shared chat database](/conventions/web-ui/index.html#the-sqlite-store). Any other value is the name of a class that implements `INotesProvider` and is created with `( config, agentName )`, for a notes service of your own. |
| `user.limit`    | 1400     | Characters of notes about the user, a whole number from 100 to 20000. Each user has their own.                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `agent.limit`   | 2200     | Characters of notes about the agent's work, a whole number from 100 to 20000. Shared by everyone who talks to it.                                                                                                                                                     |
| `tool`          | `true`   | `remember` (save or replace a note) and `forget` (remove one). Without them the notes are read-only for the agent and a person manages them.                                                                                                                          |
| `approveForget` | `true`   | A run that wants to `forget` stops for [approval](/cli-reference/index.html#chat), like any tool that needs it. Saving a note needs none.                                                                                                                             |

How it works:

* Both scopes go into the system prompt as short lists, oldest first, within their limits. They are read once per conversation, so the prompt stays the same turn to turn (a provider's prompt cache keeps working) and a note saved now shows from the next conversation.
* A note is one line of at most 500 characters. Nothing is dropped silently: a note that does not fit the limit is refused, and the agent is told how full the notes are so it can replace or forget an older one.
* **Who a user is** : it is the name of the [access token](/conventions/agent-bx/index.html#access-tokens-for-a-deployed-agent) the caller used, or `local` when the route is open. `local` is also who you are in `bxAgents chat` (`--user=NAME` changes it), so the terminal, the web page and the API share one set of conversations and notes on an open server. The agent scope belongs to the agent's `name`.
* The terminal chat, the web chat and the server share one file, `data/chat.db` (see [the SQLite store](/conventions/web-ui/index.html#the-sqlite-store)).

Manage them yourself with `/remember` and `/notes` in [`chat`](/cli-reference/index.html#chat), with [`bxAgents notes`](/cli-reference/index.html#notes) from a shell, or over HTTP through the [run-control routes](/conventions/agent-bx/index.html#run-control).

## Instructions

The agent's instructions are its system prompt. Put them in an `instructions.md` beside `Agent.yaml`, the usual choice because the file is plain Markdown and easy to edit:

    my-agent/
    ├── Agent.yaml
    └── instructions.md

For a short prompt you can write them inline instead:

```yaml
name: greeter
model: openai/gpt-5
instructions: |
  You greet people by name.
  Keep it to one sentence.
```

If both exist, **`instructions.md` wins** - the file is the more deliberate choice, so a stray `instructions:` line cannot override it. If neither exists, `build` fails and says so.

## Environments

`environments` holds overrides keyed by environment name. It is the YAML spelling of the environment-override methods (`production()`) an `Agent.bx` can declare:

```yaml
name: support
model: openai/gpt-5

environments:
  production:
    model: openai/gpt-5-mini
  staging:
    description: Staging copy
```

The active environment is chosen with this precedence, highest first:

1. the `--environment` CLI flag (`bxAgents build --environment=production`)
2. the `BX_AGENTS_ENV` environment variable
3. `development`

Only the block for the active environment is applied, on top of the top-level settings; keys it does not mention are left alone. Each block accepts the same keys as the top level, except `environments` itself.

`bxAgents test` builds against the `test` environment, which is why a scaffolded project carries a `test` block pointing at the `mock` provider: its tests need no API key or network access.
> **Note**
>
> An `Agent.yaml` cannot compute its environment. The `detectEnvironment()` method described under [Environment overrides](/conventions/agent-bx/index.html#environment-overrides) needs code, so a project that needs it uses an `Agent.bx`.

The overrides then merge with `boxlang.json`, `boxlang-{environment}.json`, `miniserver.json` and `miniserver-{environment}.json` exactly as described in [Merge semantics](/conventions/agent-bx/index.html#merge-semantics).

## Requirements

Reading YAML needs the `bx-yaml` module, **1.1.0 or later** . BxAgents bundles it, so there is nothing to install. Global YAML tags (such as `!!java.io.File`) are rejected, so a cloned project's `Agent.yaml` cannot make the build instantiate arbitrary Java classes.

## YAML or Agent.bx?

|                      Use                       |                                                                   When                                                                   |
|------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `Agent.yaml`                                   | The agent is configuration: a name, a model, instructions, memory, subagents. This is almost every agent.                                |
| [`Agent.bx`](/conventions/agent-bx/index.html) | The definition itself needs code: hooks, dynamic instructions, tools registered in code, an overridden method, or `detectEnvironment()`. |

You can start with YAML and switch later: create the `Agent.bx`, move the settings across, and delete the `Agent.yaml`.

title: Application.bx
body: Application.bx A project has its own Application.bx at its root. It is the file the runtime loads, so the settings and lifecycle hooks of your app live here. It extends a class BxAgents generates on every build, which holds the wiring: // Application.bx class extends="bxagents.Application" { } bxAgents new writes this file. Build copies it into the generated app as it is. A project without one gets exactly this file generated, so older projects keep building. What the generated base does On every build bxagents/Application.bx is written into .build/app/ and sets up: the app name , sessions (on when there is a web UI) and the web UI's database; ColdBox, started from onApplicationStart() , with the bx-ai settings applied first; tools, MCP servers, gateways and interceptors , registered at startup; this.schedulers , listing the project's schedules/ . It starts with a comment saying it is generated. Do not edit it: the next build overwrites it. Override a hook, or add a setting Your class loads after the base's, so a setting you assign wins, and a method you define replaces the base's. To add to a hook instead of replacing it, call super : // Application.bx class extends="bxagents.Application" { this.sessionTimeout = createTimeSpan( 0, 4, 0, 0 ) function onApplicationStart() { var started = super.onApplicationStart() application.startedAt = now() return started } } Warning Replacing onApplicationStart() or onRequestStart() without calling super removes the wiring above (ColdBox never starts). Always call the super method unless that is what you mean. The bxagents mapping bxagents.Application and bxagents.Scheduler resolve to the bxagents/ folder inside the built app, so the files they extend are copied with it and nothing depends on the module being installed where the app runs. Runtime helpers that the built app needs live there. The folder exists after a build. Before the first bxAgents build , an IDE cannot follow bxagents.Application ; the class itself is not in your project. Paths The base lives one folder down, so it resolves paths from the app folder, not from its own location. If you write code in Application.bx that reads a file, use expandPath( "/..." ) from the app root.
headings: Override a hook, or add a setting

# box.json

BxAgents already bundles BX AI, ColdBox and the other modules agents use, so most agents need nothing more. When an agent needs a package that is not bundled, for example `bx-playwright` for browser tools, list it in a `box.json` at the project root and install it yourself:

```json
{
  "name": "support-bot",
  "dependencies": {
    "bx-playwright": "*"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "testbox": "*"
  }
}
```

BxAgents never installs anything. Install packages the way you normally do, with CommandBox (`box install`) or the BoxLang binary (`install-bx-module bx-playwright --local`), from the project root. `bxAgents new` scaffolds a `box.json` for you, with TestBox as a development dependency installed into `lib/testbox`, and a `.gitignore` that already ignores `lib/` and `boxlang_modules/`. Commit `box.json`; keep the installed folders out of version control.

## Where installed packages go

|                  What                  |        Folder in the project        |                                                                                  What `build` does with it                                                                                   |
|----------------------------------------|-------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| BoxLang modules (`bx-playwright`, ...) | `boxlang_modules/`                  | BoxLang loads this folder from the project root, so `chat`, `invoke` and `test` find them. `build` copies it to `.build/app/boxlang_modules`, so `serve` and a packaged `.bxa` carry it too. |
| ColdBox libraries and modules          | `lib/coldbox`, `lib/modules/<name>` | Copied into the app over the bundled ones, so a project can add or override a library.                                                                                                       |
| Test tools (TestBox, ...)              | `lib/<name>` or `tests/`            | Not copied: the app does not need them.                                                                                                                                                      |

## Development dependencies

A BoxLang module that is only in `devDependencies` is left out of `.build/app`, and the build says which. A module is matched to `box.json` by the `slug` in its own `box.json`, or by its folder name (`bxplaywright` for `bx-playwright`). One listed in both sections is kept.

## Using an installed module

A module that registers tools, such as `bx-playwright`, is used by naming its tools in the agent's [`tools`](/conventions/agent-yaml/index.html#tools). If the module is not installed, the error says how to install it:

```yaml
tools:
  - "*@bxplaywright"
```

> **Note**
>
> `box.json` is different from [`modules/`](/conventions/modules/index.html), which holds ColdBox modules that are part of your project's own source.

markdown:
# Call your agent from code

Every built agent serves one HTTP API at `/__bxagents`. The web chat page, the terminal chat and the gateways use the same one, so anything they do, your program can do. This guide is the tour; every route, with its request and answer, is in the [OpenAPI document](#the-openapi-document) the server hands out, and the settings are in [agentApi](/conventions/agent-bx/index.html#the-always-on-agent-route).

*Two and a half minutes: open mode and its startup warning, token mode, the guards, the BoxLang client, the OpenAPI document, the web page, the terminal chat and gateway sessions. The agent answers are canned (the mock provider), and the gateway part runs the gateway session tests.*

The project in [`examples/api-agent/`](https://github.com/ortus-boxlang/bx-agents/tree/development/examples/api-agent) runs everything below.

## Open or behind a token

Two ways to run, chosen by `agentApi` in `Agent.yaml`.

|                    |                    Settings                     |                                                                        Who may call                                                                         |
|--------------------|-------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Open (the default) | nothing                                         | Anyone who can reach the port. Everyone is one user, `local`. Keep it on `127.0.0.1`; `serve` prints a warning when an open API listens on every interface. |
| Token              | `tokenEnvVar: MY_SECRET`, and/or `tokens: true` | Callers that send `x-bxagents-token`. The shared secret is an admin; issued tokens are `chat` or `admin`. Everything else gets `401`.                       |

You can also narrow who may call with `allowedIPs` and cap how often with `rateLimit`; both work open or closed.

```yaml
agentApi:
  tokenEnvVar: TOKEN_FOR_ADMIN   # the NAME of an environment variable
  tokens: true                   # also accept tokens made with `bxAgents token create`
  manageTokens: true             # an admin may make and revoke tokens over the API
```

## Connections

When an `mcpServers` entry has `oauth` ([connect](/conventions/connect/index.html)), the API has the sign in routes. They act for the caller: nothing a caller sends can name somebody else.

|          Route          |                                                                                                                         |
|-------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `GET /connect`          | The services, and whether the caller is connected to each. Never a token                                                |
| `POST /connect`         | `{ "name": "mail" }` starts a sign in and answers `{ "authorizationUrl" }` to send the caller to                        |
| `POST /connect/remove`  | `{ "name": "mail" }` forgets the caller's sign in                                                                       |
| `GET /connect/callback` | Where the provider sends the browser back. **Open** , because the single use `state` says who it is. Shows a small page |

## With curl

```bash
export T="x-bxagents-token: $TOKEN_FOR_ADMIN"

curl -H "$T" http://127.0.0.1:8080/__bxagents/whoami

curl -H "$T" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"input":"What can you do?"}' \
     http://127.0.0.1:8080/__bxagents/invoke
```

`invoke` answers `{ "success": true, "output": "...", "threadId": "..." }`. Send `conversationId` to carry on a conversation; the agent remembers it for you.

## With BoxLang

```javascript
import bxModules.bxagents.models.api.AgentApiClient;

agentClient = new AgentApiClient( url = "http://127.0.0.1:8080", token = getSystemSetting( "TOKEN_FOR_ADMIN" ) );

first = agentClient.invoke( "What can you do?" );
println( first.output );

// the text as it is written
agentClient.stream( "Say it shorter.", ( text ) => print( text ), first.threadId );
```

Build the client with named arguments. There is one method for each route: `invoke`, `stream`, `events`, `resume`, `cancel`, `steer`, `sessions`, `history`, `export`, `notes`, `preferences`, `command`, `tokens` and the rest. A bad request comes back as `{ success: false, error, code }`; a refused token, a missing route or a server failure is thrown. Pass `path` when the server moved the API with `agentApi.path`, and `source` to name your program in the conversation list.

## Streams

`stream` and `events` answer server-sent events: each frame is `event: <name>` then `data: <json>`.

|    Frame    |                              Meaning                               |
|-------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `thread`    | First frame: the run's id, for `cancel`, `steer` and `resume`.     |
| `chunk`     | A piece of what the model is saying.                               |
| `tool`      | A tool call started (`running`) or finished (`ok`). `events` only. |
| `suspended` | The run paused for approval. Answer with `resume`. `events` only.  |
| `error`     | The run failed.                                                    |
| `done`      | Last frame.                                                        |

`stream` carries `thread`, `chunk` and `done`. `events` carries all of them, and the client turns them into events for your callback: `thread`, `delta`, `reasoning`, `tool`, `suspended`, `error`.

## Run control

A run belongs to the caller who started it.

|                           Call                           |                          Does                          |
|----------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
| `cancel( threadId )`                                     | Stops it. Only its owner, or an admin.                 |
| `steer( threadId, input )`                               | Adds a message to a run that is going.                 |
| `pending( threadId )` and `resume( threadId, decision )` | Approve, reject or edit what a paused run wants to do. |

## Conversations, notes and settings

Conversations belong to the caller too: `sessions()` lists them, newest first (an admin may pass `all = true` for everyone's), and `createSession`, `renameSession`, `forkSession`, `deleteSession`, `history` and `export` work on one. `notes()` and `preferences()` keep what the agent should remember about the caller. `command( "/context" )` runs any [slash command](/guides/slash-commands/index.html) the caller may use.

## Access tokens over the API

With `manageTokens: true` an admin can make tokens without a shell on the server:

```javascript
made = agentClient.createToken( name = "ci", scope = "chat", expires = "90d" );
println( made.token );        // shown once; the server keeps only a fingerprint
agentClient.revokeToken( "ci" );
```

The same list, create and revoke are in the **Tokens** panel of the [web page](/conventions/web-ui/index.html) (shown to admins on a server that allows it). A `chat` token gets `403`. Leave `manageTokens` off and the routes do not exist.

## Errors

Every error is `{ "success": false, "error": "text for people", "code": "machine_code" }`.

| Status |                                                                            Codes                                                                            |
|--------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 400    | `bad_request`, `bad_profile`, `bad_attachment`                                                                                                              |
| 401    | `unauthorized`                                                                                                                                              |
| 403    | `forbidden`, `csrf`, `not_your_run`                                                                                                                         |
| 404    | `not_found`, `no_notes`                                                                                                                                     |
| 405    | `method_not_allowed`                                                                                                                                        |
| 409    | `busy` (a run is already going in that conversation)                                                                                                        |
| 429    | `rate_limited` from a token check; the `rateLimit` guard (cbSecurity's Throttle) answers `{ "error": true, "messages": [...] }` with a `Retry-After` header |

## The OpenAPI document

```bash
curl -H "$T" http://127.0.0.1:8080/__bxagents/openapi > agent-api.json
```

It is an OpenAPI 3 document of the routes this server really has: every route, what it takes and answers, the token header on a closed API, and the stream frames. Feed it to a client generator or an API tool such as Swagger UI or Postman. The routes, the document and the BoxLang client are all made from one list, and a test fails when they disagree.

title: Chat walkthroughs
body: Chat walkthroughs Six short sessions, each about two minutes. They assume an agent you have already built; if you have not, start with the quick start . Every key and command used here is listed in The terminal UI and Slash commands . The keys, prompt styles, context, name, fork and sessions in one run. The answers in these recordings come from a scripted demo model, so they are canned. Everything else is the real screen. 1. Your first conversation bxAgents build bxAgents chat Type a question and press Enter . The answer streams in; any tool the agent calls is shown with its arguments and how long it took. Press Alt+Enter for a second line before sending. Type / and look at the menu, or ? for the keys. Type /tools to see what the agent can call. Press Esc while the agent is working to stop it at its next step. Type while it works to steer it: your message is added to the run. /copy puts the last answer on the clipboard. /exit , or Ctrl+C on an empty box, to leave. Scroll up afterwards: the conversation is ordinary terminal text. 2. Pick a conversation up again bxAgents chat --continue # the latest one, with its history Inside a chat: /name Quarterly plan names this conversation. /fork Other approach copies it, messages and all, and carries on in the copy. The original stays as it was. /sessions lists your conversations, numbered. /resume 2 goes back to number 2 and shows what was said. /export plan.html saves the conversation as a page. A .md name saves Markdown. After /name and /fork : three conversations, numbered, with their message counts. Messages are kept in the agent's memory , so a conversation can be picked up again only as far as that memory lasts. The default cache memory is lost when the process ends; a file or jdbc memory is not. 3. Try another model Needs more than one profile in the project. /model shows the model in use. /profile lists the profiles; pick one with the arrows. Or /profile fast goes straight to it. The conversation, tools and instructions stay; only the model changes. /ping checks the model answers, and says how long it took or why it did not. /default goes back to the app's default. 4. Notes the agent keeps Needs a notes block in Agent.yaml . /remember I prefer short answers keeps a note about you. The agent sees it in every conversation. /notes opens the notes screen. a adds, e edits, d removes (after a yes), Tab switches between your notes and the agent's, Esc goes back. /notes stats shows how many characters you use of the limit and the rough tokens they add to every conversation. 5. Show it a file or a picture Type @ and a list of files under your folder opens. Keep typing to narrow it; Tab takes one. The file's content goes with your message. @diagram.png sends a picture. A profile that sets vision: false makes the chat refuse it with a message instead of a provider error. Ctrl+V pastes a picture from the clipboard. !git diff --stat runs a command on your machine and sends what it printed along with your next message. !! shows it without sending. /context shows how big the context is and what it is made of: system prompt, tool definitions, notes and messages. The output of a !command waiting for your next message counts too. 6. # Chat walkthroughs

Six short sessions, each about two minutes. They assume an agent you have already built; if you have not, start with the [quick start](/getting-started/quick-start/index.html). Every key and command used here is listed in [The terminal UI](/guides/terminal-ui/index.html) and [Slash commands](/guides/slash-commands/index.html).

*The keys, prompt styles, context, name, fork and sessions in one run. The answers in these recordings come from a scripted demo model, so they are canned. Everything else is the real screen.*

## 1. Your first conversation

```bash
bxAgents build
bxAgents chat
```

1. Type a question and press **Enter**. The answer streams in; any tool the agent calls is shown with its arguments and how long it took.
2. Press **Alt+Enter** for a second line before sending.
3. Type `/` and look at the menu, or `?` for the keys. Type `/tools` to see what the agent can call.
4. Press **Esc** while the agent is working to stop it at its next step. Type while it works to **steer** it: your message is added to the run.
5. `/copy` puts the last answer on the clipboard.
6. `/exit`, or **Ctrl+C** on an empty box, to leave.

Scroll up afterwards: the conversation is ordinary terminal text.

## 2. Pick a conversation up again

```bash
bxAgents chat --continue          # the latest one, with its history
```

Inside a chat:

1. `/name Quarterly plan` names this conversation.
2. `/fork Other approach` copies it, messages and all, and carries on in the copy. The original stays as it was.
3. `/sessions` lists your conversations, numbered. `/resume 2` goes back to number 2 and shows what was said.
4. `/export plan.html` saves the conversation as a page. A `.md` name saves Markdown.

![The conversation list after naming and forking](/assets/tui/chat-sessions.png)

*After `/name` and `/fork`: three conversations, numbered, with their message counts.*

Messages are kept in the agent's [memory](/conventions/agent-yaml/index.html#settings), so a conversation can be picked up again only as far as that memory lasts. The default `cache` memory is lost when the process ends; a `file` or `jdbc` memory is not.

## 3. Try another model

Needs more than one [profile](/conventions/models/index.html#profiles) in the project.

1. `/model` shows the model in use.
2. `/profile` lists the profiles; pick one with the arrows. Or `/profile fast` goes straight to it. The conversation, tools and instructions stay; only the model changes.
3. `/ping` checks the model answers, and says how long it took or why it did not.
4. `/default` goes back to the app's default.

## 4. Notes the agent keeps

Needs a [`notes`](/conventions/agent-yaml/index.html#notes) block in `Agent.yaml`.

1. `/remember I prefer short answers` keeps a note about you. The agent sees it in every conversation.
2. `/notes` opens the notes screen. **a** adds, **e** edits, **d** removes (after a yes), **Tab** switches between your notes and the agent's, **Esc** goes back.
3. `/notes stats` shows how many characters you use of the limit and the rough tokens they add to every conversation.

## 5. Show it a file or a picture

1. Type `@` and a list of files under your folder opens. Keep typing to narrow it; **Tab** takes one. The file's content goes with your message.
2. `@diagram.png` sends a picture. A profile that sets `vision: false` makes the chat refuse it with a message instead of a provider error.
3. **Ctrl+V** pastes a picture from the clipboard.
4. `!git diff --stat` runs a command on your machine and sends what it printed along with your next message. `!!` shows it without sending.
5. `/context` shows how big the context is and what it is made of: system prompt, tool definitions, notes and messages. The output of a `!command` waiting for your next message counts too.

## 6. Make the chat your own

1. `/prompt` shows the message box looks and widgets. `/prompt box` changes the look and `/prompt top +git -clock` changes the top bar, for this chat only. To set it for the project, use a [`tui:` block](/guides/terminal-ui/index.html#the-look-of-the-message-box) in `Agent.yaml`.
2. `?` alone, or `/keys`, lists every key with its action name. To change one, put it in `~/.bxagents/bxAgents.yml`: `chat:` then `keys:` then, for example, `newline: ctrl+n`. See [Change a key](/guides/terminal-ui/index.html#change-a-key).
3. `/extensions` lists what the [extensions](/guides/first-extension/index.html) added: commands, keys and more. After you edit one, `/reload` loads it again without leaving the chat.
4. `/record demo.cast` starts saving the screen as an asciicast file, and `/record stop` ends it. Or start with `bxAgents chat --record=demo.cast`.
5. `/stats` shows the tokens the model calls used, once `usage: true` is set in `Agent.yaml`. `/stats enable` writes that line for you.

## The wizard in the same style

*The `new` wizard from the name to the finished project.*

`bxAgents new my-agent` is the other screen. Arrow keys or `j`/`k` move, **Space** ticks, **Enter** confirms, **Esc** goes back one question and **Ctrl+C** cancels without creating anything. The last screen prints the one-line command that would build the same project with no questions. The full tour is in [the new wizard](/guides/new-wizard/index.html).
