markdown:
# schedules/

Every `schedules/*.bx` is a **BoxLang scheduler** : a plain class whose `configure()` builds tasks with BoxLang's own task DSL. There is no ColdBox in it and nothing to extend:

```javascript
// schedules/Nightly.bx
class {

	function configure() {
		task( "cleanup" )
			.cron( "0 0 * * *" )
			.call( () => run( "clean up old tickets" ) )
			.withNoOverlaps()
	}

}
```

The build copies each file into the app as `schedules/<Name>.bx`, lists them in `this.schedulers` of the [generated base `Application`](/conventions/application-bx/index.html), and BoxLang starts them with the app and stops them with it. They run while the app is served (`bxAgents serve`).
> **Note**
>
> A scheduler is for the developer. For prompts that the people who use the agent make for themselves, by asking it, see [routines](/conventions/routines/index.html).
> **Tip**
>
> `bxAgents add schedule` writes one for you: say when it runs, what to tell the agent, and which agent. See [`add`](/cli-reference/index.html#add-schedule).

## What you get without writing an `extends`

The build adds `extends="bxagents.Scheduler"` to any scheduler class that names no parent of its own. That class is copied into the app (`bxagents/Scheduler.bx`) and gives your scheduler these methods:

|             Method              |                                                                 What it does                                                                  |
|---------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `task( name )`                  | BoxLang's task builder: `.cron()`, `.every()`, `.everyDayAt()`, `.withNoOverlaps()`, `.call()` ...                                            |
| `run( input, params, options )` | Sends a message to the **default agent** , the root agent your `Agent.yaml` or `Agent.bx` defines. Takes the agent's own `run()` arguments.   |
| `agent( name )`                 | Any agent in the project tree by the `name` its own definition declares, root or subagent at any depth. With no name it is the default agent. |
| `defaultAgent()`                | The root agent.                                                                                                                               |
| `getInstance( dsl )`            | WireBox's `getInstance()`, for anything else the app registered.                                                                              |
| `controller()`                  | The running ColdBox controller.                                                                                                               |

```javascript
// schedules/Digest.bx
class {

	function configure() {
		task( "weekly-digest" )
			.cron( "0 8 * * MON" )
			.call( () => agent( "ResearchBot" ).run( "summarize this week's findings" ) )
	}

}
```

Everything is reached when a task fires, not when `configure()` runs, so a scheduler can be configured before ColdBox has finished starting.

If a class names a parent already (`class extends="my.BaseScheduler" {`), the build leaves it alone. Make your parent extend `bxagents.Scheduler` to keep the methods above.

## Cron

`.cron( "..." )` is BoxLang's own and takes **5 fields** (`minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week`) or **6 fields** with seconds in front:

```javascript
.cron( "*/15 * * * *" )        // every 15 minutes
.cron( "0 9 * * 1-5" )         // 09:00 on weekdays
.cron( "0 30 8 * * MON-FRI" )  // 08:30:00 on weekdays (six fields)
```

Lists (`1,3,5`), ranges (`1-5`), steps (`*/5`), month names (`JAN`) and day names (`MON`) work. Anything else the task DSL offers is there too: `.every( 15, "minutes" )`, `.everyDayAt( "09:00" )`, `.onWeekdays( "08:30" )`, `.onFirstBusinessDayOfTheMonth( "09:00" )`, `.startOn()`, `.endOn()`, `.when()`, `.withNoOverlaps()`, `.onSuccess()`, `.onFailure()`, timezones.

## Retrieving an agent

Every agent in the project's tree is registered in the generated `config/WireBox.bx` under its own declared `name`. `agent( "ResearchBot" )` resolves it, and `run( ... )` is the root agent. Because `name` is also a WireBox binding key it must be **unique across the whole project** - `build` fails validation if two agents share one. See [subagents/](/conventions/subagents/index.html#retrieving-an-agent-from-schedules).

```yaml
# subagents/researcher/Agent.yaml
name: ResearchBot
model: openai/gpt-5
```

## Validation

`build` checks, because each would otherwise only fail when the app starts:

* the file name becomes the class name (`schedules.<Name>`), so it must be letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter or underscore. `my-job.bx` is refused; `MyJob.bx` is fine;
* two files that would make the same scheduler class are refused: rename one;
* a scheduler that extends `coldbox.system.web.tasks.ColdBoxScheduler` is refused, with what to change;
* a file in `schedules/` that is not a `.bx` file is ignored, with a warning so a schedule that quietly stopped running is visible.

A syntax error or a wrong agent name in the body surfaces when the app starts (`serve`), like any other BoxLang class.
> **ColdBox's scheduler is a separate thing**
>
> Chat-platform [gateways](/conventions/gateways/index.html) register their polling tasks with ColdBox's own app scheduler. That is untouched, and a project's `schedules/` never go through it.

body:
skills/ Each immediate subfolder of skills/ that contains a SKILL.md file is one skill, following the Claude Agent Skills convention: YAML frontmatter ( name , description ) followed by a body of freeform instructions. skills/ └── greeting/ └── SKILL.md --- name: greeting description: How to greet people warmly. --- Always greet the user warmly and use their name if known. Tip bxAgents add skill creates skills//SKILL.md with the frontmatter and a body to fill in. See add . Naming The skill's name is its frontmatter name: if present; otherwise it falls back to the folder name ( greeting/ with no frontmatter name would be discovered as greeting anyway, but an explicit name: always wins even if it differs from the folder). Two skills resolving to the same name fail validation with a duplicate-name error. A folder without a SKILL.md inside it is not discovered as a skill at all - it's simply ignored (useful for scratch subfolders, assets kept alongside a skill under a different structure, etc., as long as they don't sit directly under skills/ themselves without a SKILL.md ). # skills/ Each immediate subfolder of `skills/` that contains a `SKILL.md` file is one skill, following the Claude Agent Skills convention: YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) followed by a body of freeform instructions. skills/ └── greeting/ └── SKILL.md ```markdown --- name: greeting description: How to greet people warmly. --- Always greet the user warmly and use their name if known. ``` > **Tip** > > `bxAgents add skill ` creates `skills//SKILL.md` with the frontmatter and a body to fill in. See [`add`](/cli-reference/index.html#add-skill). ## Naming The skill's name is its frontmatter `name:` if present; otherwise it falls back to the folder name (`greeting/` with no frontmatter name would be discovered as `greeting` anyway, but an explicit `name:` always wins even if it differs from the folder). Two skills resolving to the same name fail validation with a duplicate-name error. A folder without a `SKILL.md` inside it is not discovered as a skill at all - it's simply ignored (useful for scratch subfolders, assets kept alongside a skill under a different structure, etc., as long as they don't sit directly under `skills/` themselves without a `SKILL.md`). ## The three levels An agent's skill list is made from three levels. The first two are built into the app; the third is written by the agent while it runs. ```mermaid flowchart TB GL["Global skills folder
managed by a skills tool (npx, CommandBox)"] subgraph project["Your project"] direction TB INS[".agents/skills/
1. Installed
links to the global folder, or installed copies"] SHIP["skills/
2. Ships with the agent
written by you"] end subgraph app["The built app: skills/"] direction TB A1["copies of the installed skills
listed in .installed.json"] A2["copies of your skills"] end subgraph home["The data home: skills/"] DH["3. The agent's own
written by the agent with skill_save"] end LIST(["The agent's skill list
loaded by name when a task needs one"]) GL -. "symbolic link" .-> INS INS -->|build| A1 SHIP -->|build| A2 A1 --> LIST A2 --> LIST DH -->|"at start, and the moment it is saved"| LIST ``` | Level | Where | Written by | `origin` in `/skills` | |-------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------|-----------------------| | 1. Installed | `.agents/skills/` in the project. A skills tool links a skill from its global folder into it, or `bxAgents skills install` copies one there. It stays out of source control and is restored at build time | A skills tool or the registry | `installed` | | 2. Ships with the agent | `skills/` in the project, and the skills [extensions](/conventions/extensions/index.html) carry | You | `project` | | 3. The agent's own | `skills/` in the [data home](/conventions/data/index.html#skills-the-agent-saves) | The agent, with its `skill_save` tool | `agent` | The rules between the levels: * **Yours wins over installed.** A skill in `skills/` and an installed one with the same name or folder: the one in `skills/` is used. * **The agent never replaces the first two.** `skill_save` refuses the name of an installed skill or one that ships with the agent. It can save over a skill it wrote itself, to improve it. * **A link is followed.** The app gets a copy of what the link points at, so a deployed app does not depend on the global folder. * **The app tells levels 1 and 2 apart** by `skills/.installed.json`, which the build writes beside the skills. `/skills` and `GET /skills` use it to show each skill's level. Level 3 is described in [data and volumes](/conventions/data/index.html#skills-the-agent-saves): approval of each save, the limits, and the `skills` setting in `Agent.yaml`. ## Skills from the registry Skills from skills.boxlang.io are installed with `bxAgents skills install `, not copied by hand. They go in `.agents/skills/` (bx-ai's own default folder), out of source control; `.agents/skills.lock.json` is committed and `build` restores from it. Both folders go into the build, and a skill in `skills/` with the same name wins. A global skills tool can link its skills into `.agents/skills/` instead; a link is followed and the app gets a copy. See [`skills`](/cli-reference/index.html#skills). ## How it's wired at runtime `skills/` is copied verbatim into the generated app (same wipe-then-write, dotfile-excluding copy as [`tools/`](/conventions/tools/index.html)). The generated app always points bx-ai's own `skillsDirectory` module setting at `/skills`. It is written to `config/bxai-settings.json` (not `config/ColdBox.bx`, because ColdBox's `moduleSettings` does not reach bx-ai, a BoxLang module) and applied when the app starts: ```json { "skillsDirectory": "/skills" } ``` > **Info** > > bx-ai's own default `skillsDirectory` is `/.agents/skills` - a different path than BxAgents' `skills/` convention. The generator always overrides it explicitly so the app's `skills/` folder is the one bx-ai actually loads from. Skills installed under your project's `.agents/skills/` are copied into it at build time; you never need to set this yourself.

markdown:
# Slash commands

Type `/` in the terminal chat or the [web chat](/conventions/web-ui/index.html#slash-commands) to see the commands. Each one is written once, as a small class that answers with data, and every surface draws that answer its own way. In [chat platforms](/conventions/gateways/index.html#commands-in-a-gateway) type the command as a message; the default prefix is `/` and a gateway can change it.

**Where** is `T` terminal, `W` web page, `G` chat platforms. A command marked `G` still needs to be in the gateway's `allow` list; the default list is `help`, `info`, `tools`, `model`, `ping`, `notes` and `remember`.

![/sessions after naming and forking a conversation](/assets/tui/chat-sessions.png)

*`/name`, `/fork` and `/sessions` in a real chat.*

## Conversations

|               Command                | Where |                                                                              Does                                                                               |        Example         |
|--------------------------------------|-------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------|
| `/new`                               | T W G | Start a new conversation. The old one stays in the list                                                                                                         | `/new`                 |
| `/sessions`                          | T W G | List your recent conversations, numbered                                                                                                                        | `/sessions`            |
| `/resume [number or id]`             | T W G | Go back to one and show what was said. No argument: the most recent                                                                                             | `/resume 2`            |
| `/name <name>`                       | T W   | Name this conversation                                                                                                                                          | `/name Quarterly plan` |
| `/fork [name]`                       | T W   | Copy this conversation, messages and all, and carry on in the copy                                                                                              | `/fork Other approach` |
| `/clear`                             | T W G | Forget this conversation's messages, keep the conversation                                                                                                      | `/clear`               |
| `/compact`                           | T W G | Replace older messages with a summary and keep the latest few (`keepRecent`). The agent's own model writes the summary, unless its memory names a summary model | `/compact`             |
| `/export [file] [--format=md\|html]` | T W   | Save the conversation. The file name decides the format unless `--format` says                                                                                  | `/export plan.html`    |
| `/exit` (alias `/quit`)              | T     | Leave the chat                                                                                                                                                  | `/exit`                |

On a gateway, `/new`, `/clear`, `/compact`, `/sessions` and `/resume` are off until the gateway sets `commands.conversation: true`.

## Know what is going on

|                      Command                      | Where |                                                                                       Does                                                                                       |       Example       |
|---------------------------------------------------|-------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------|
| `/help`                                           | T W G | List the commands you can run here                                                                                                                                               | `/help`             |
| `/info`                                           | T W G | Agent, model, conversation, message count, notes and database                                                                                                                    | `/info`             |
| `/tools`                                          | T W G | List the agent's tools                                                                                                                                                           | `/tools`            |
| `/skills`                                         | T W G | List the skills the agent can load, and its level: installed, project or agent                                                                                                   | `/skills`           |
| `/context`                                        | T W   | How big the context is and what it is made of, and how many of the messages its memory keeps this conversation has (a warning near the limit). Worked out locally, no model call | `/context`          |
| `/stats [days] [--by=model\|provider\|day\|user]` | T     | Tokens the model calls used. `/stats enable` turns usage recording on                                                                                                            | `/stats 7 --by=day` |
| `/keys`                                           | T W   | Which key does what, with the action name of each. `?` alone does the same                                                                                                       | `/keys`             |

## Models

|      Command      | Where |                                                            Does                                                            |     Example     |
|-------------------|-------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------|
| `/model`          | T W G | Show the model in use, its profile, context window and vision support                                                      | `/model`        |
| `/profile [name]` | T     | Pick a [profile](/conventions/models/index.html#profiles) from a list, or switch straight to one. The conversation is kept | `/profile fast` |
| `/default`        | T     | Go back to the app's default model                                                                                         | `/default`      |
| `/ping [profile]` | T W G | Test that the model answers, with one tiny question. Says how long it took, or why it did not                              | `/ping fast`    |

Over `--connect` or `--server`, `/profile` can only switch among the profiles the server lists in [`agentApi.profiles`](/conventions/agent-bx/index.html#agentapi).

## Notes

|           Command           | Where |                                                                     Does                                                                     |               Example               |
|-----------------------------|-------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------|
| `/remember <text>`          | T W G | Keep a note about you                                                                                                                        | `/remember I prefer short answers`  |
| `/notes`                    | T W G | Open the notes screen (terminal)                                                                                                             | `/notes`                            |
| `/connect`                  | T W G | List the services that ask you to sign in and whether you are connected; `/connect NAME` starts a sign in, `/connect NAME remove` forgets it | `/connect mail`                     |
| `/vault`                    | T W G | Open the vault screen (terminal), or list the secret names. A value is never typed in a command                                              | `/vault`                            |
| `/notes list`               | T W G | Print your notes and the agent's, with how full each is                                                                                      | `/notes list`                       |
| `/notes add [agent] <text>` | T W G | Add a note about you, or with `agent` about the agent's work                                                                                 | `/notes add agent Use metric units` |
| `/notes edit <id> <text>`   | T W G | Change a note; the id is the short code in the list                                                                                          | `/notes edit a3f New text`          |
| `/notes remove <id>`        | T W G | Remove a note. Removing the agent's needs an `admin` token over `--connect`                                                                  | `/notes remove a3f`                 |
| `/notes stats`              | T W G | Characters used against the limit, and the rough tokens they add                                                                             | `/notes stats`                      |

## Your terminal

These act on your own machine or your own session, so they stay in the terminal (`/extensions` also works in the web page).

|             Command              | Where |                                        Does                                        |                 Example                  |
|----------------------------------|-------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------|
| `/extensions [name]`             | T W   | List the extensions the chat loads and what each added; with a name, one in detail | `/extensions`                            |
| `/reload`                        | T     | Load the extensions and their settings again. Admin only                           | `/reload`                                |
| `/prompt [style]`                | T     | Show or change the message box look for this chat                                  | `/prompt box`, `/prompt top +git -clock` |
| `/copy`                          | T     | Copy the last answer to the clipboard (OSC 52, honoured by most terminals)         | `/copy`                                  |
| `/record [file]`, `/record stop` | T     | Record the screen as a `.cast` file                                                | `/record demo.cast`                      |

## Add your own

`/extensions` and `/reload` come with the [extension](/conventions/extensions/index.html) support. An extension adds commands such as `/deploy` or `/roll 2d6` to the chat, and [a first extension](/guides/first-extension/index.html) walks through one. The commands over HTTP are `GET /__bxagents/commands` and `POST /__bxagents/command`, see [Run control](/conventions/agent-bx/index.html#run-control).

title: subagents/
body:
subagents/ subagents/ holds nested agents, each an ordinary BxAgents project of its own - an Agent.yaml + instructions.md (and optionally its own tools/ , skills/ , etc.). A subagent's tools/ belong to it alone, and its tools: list is its own; neither is inherited from or shared with its parent: my-agent/ ├── Agent.yaml # subAgents: [ researcher ] ├── instructions.md └── subagents/ └── researcher/ ├── Agent.yaml └── instructions.md A subagent is wired to its parent by name, declared in the parent's Agent.yaml subAgents list - the subagents/ FOLDER name to wire at build time: # Agent.yaml name: my-agent model: openai/gpt-5 subAgents: - researcher The same list in a class-based Agent.bx (the advanced form ) goes in configure() , distinct from super.init() 's own subAgents argument (which takes already-built AiAgent instances, not names). A project can mix the two forms: a YAML root with a class subagent, or the reverse. At build time, bx-ai's addSubAgent() wraps each built subagent instance as a callable tool on the parent automatically - there's no separate tool-wrapping step to write yourself. Tip bxAgents add subagent creates the folder, asks the same questions as new for its model and tools, and adds it to the parent's subAgents . --parent= nests it under another subagent. See add . Flat namespace, sibling references Every subagent - no matter how deeply another subagent's own config references it - lives directly under the root project's subagents/ folder. A subagent's own declared subAgents names reference sibling entries in that same root-level folder, not a folder nested under itself. This keeps the discovery/validation model simple: one flat directed graph over subagents/ 's immediate subfolders, rather than a tree that could nest arbitrarily deep on disk. Flat on disk, a graph in config, built bottom-up - the three views of the same project: flowchart LR subgraph disk["ON DISK - always flat, one level under the ROOT project"] direction TB R1["subagents/A/"] R2["subagents/B/"] R3["subagents/C/"] end subgraph declared["DECLARED - each definition's own subAgents list"] direction TB GA["A"] --> GB["B"] --> GC["C"] end subgraph built["BUILT - leaf-first, in GeneratedAgentFactory.bx"] direction TB O1["1. build C"] --> O2["2. build B
with the built C"] --> O3["3. build A
with the built B"] end disk -.->|"names resolve
against siblings"| declared declared -.->|"a parent needs its
children already built"| built style disk fill:#eef2f7,stroke:#5a6570 style declared fill:#e7f1ff,stroke:#004085 style built fill:#eaf6ec,stroke:#155724 A cycle in the declared graph ( A -> B -> A ) is rejected at validation, before any of this is generated; a diamond (two parents sharing one descendant) is fine. Build order Subagents are built leaf-first (bottom-up): if A declares subAgents: ["B"] and B declares subAgents: ["C"] , the generated GeneratedAgentFactory.bx builds C , then B (passing in the built C instance), then A (passing in the built B instance) - never the other way around, since a parent's aiAgent() call needs its children's already-built instances. Validation A subagent name in subAgents that doesn't correspond to a real subagents/{name}/ folder (holding an Agent.yaml or Agent.bx ) fails validation with a clear "references unknown subagent [...]" error - this applies to every node's subAgents list, including the root project's own definition, not just nested subagents. Circular references ( A → B → A ) are rejected at validation time, with the full cycle path reported (e.g. A -> B -> A ), before any code generation happens. A "diamond" shape - two subagents both depending on the same shared descendant - is not a cycle and builds fine; only genuine cycles are rejected. A missing Agent.yaml / Agent.bx inside a discovered subagents/* folder is reported as its own validation error, and so is a folder holding both ( BxAgents.AmbiguousAgentDefinition ) - a folder holds one definition. Every node's own DECLARED name (root + every subagent's own definition) must be unique across the whole project - see below. Retrieving an agent from schedules/ Two different names are in play, and they're not interchangeable: The folder name under subagents/ ( researcher above) is what subAgents: [ "..." ] references - it's purely a build-time wiring concern. The subagent's own declared name (its agent definition's name field, e.g. "ResearchBot" ) is what you retrieve it by at runtime - every agent in the tree (root + every subagent) is registered in config/WireBox.bx under this name, so a schedules/ scheduler reaches it with agent( "ResearchBot" ) (and any other WireBox-aware code with a plain getInstance( "ResearchBot" ) ). These two names can differ, and often will - the folder name is an implementation detail, the declared name is the one that matters everywhere else (prompts, WireBox retrieval). Because it's now also a WireBox binding key, build fails validation if two agents in the tree - however deeply nested - end up with the same declared name , including two that both leave it unset and silently share the "BxAi" default.

A project can mix the two forms: a YAML root with a class subagent, or the reverse. See [`add`](/cli-reference/index.html#add-subagent). ## Flat namespace, sibling references Every subagent - no matter how deeply another subagent's own config references it - lives directly under the **root** project's `subagents/` folder. A subagent's own declared `subAgents` names reference **sibling** entries in that same root-level folder, not a folder nested under itself. This keeps the discovery/validation model simple: one flat directed graph over `subagents/`'s immediate subfolders, rather than a tree that could nest arbitrarily deep on disk. Flat on disk, a graph in config, built bottom-up - the three views of the same project: ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph disk["ON DISK - always flat, one level under the ROOT project"] direction TB R1["subagents/A/"] R2["subagents/B/"] R3["subagents/C/"] end subgraph declared["DECLARED - each definition's own subAgents list"] direction TB GA["A"] --> GB["B"] --> GC["C"] end subgraph built["BUILT - leaf-first, in GeneratedAgentFactory.bx"] direction TB O1["1. build C"] --> O2["2. build B
with the built C"] --> O3["3. build A
with the built B"] end disk -.->|"names resolve
against siblings"| declared declared -.->|"a parent needs its
children already built"| built style disk fill:#eef2f7,stroke:#5a6570 style declared fill:#e7f1ff,stroke:#004085 style built fill:#eaf6ec,stroke:#155724 ``` A cycle in the declared graph (`A -> B -> A`) is rejected at validation, before any of this is generated; a diamond (two parents sharing one descendant) is fine. ## Build order Subagents are built **leaf-first** (bottom-up): if `A` declares `subAgents: ["B"]` and `B` declares `subAgents: ["C"]`, the generated `GeneratedAgentFactory.bx` builds `C`, then `B` (passing in the built `C` instance), then `A` (passing in the built `B` instance) - never the other way around, since a parent's `aiAgent()` call needs its children's already-built instances. ## Validation * A subagent name in `subAgents` that doesn't correspond to a real `subagents/{name}/` folder (holding an `Agent.yaml` or `Agent.bx`) fails validation with a clear "references unknown subagent \[...\]" error - this applies to **every** node's `subAgents` list, including the root project's own definition, not just nested subagents. * **Circular references** (`A` → `B` → `A`) are rejected at validation time, with the full cycle path reported (e.g. `A -> B -> A`), before any code generation happens. * A "diamond" shape - two subagents both depending on the same shared descendant - is **not** a cycle and builds fine; only genuine cycles are rejected. * A missing `Agent.yaml`/`Agent.bx` inside a discovered `subagents/*` folder is reported as its own validation error, and so is a folder holding both (`BxAgents.AmbiguousAgentDefinition`) - a folder holds one definition. * Every node's own DECLARED `name` (root + every subagent's own definition) must be unique across the whole project - see below. ## Retrieving an agent from `schedules/` Two different names are in play, and they're not interchangeable: * The **folder name** under `subagents/` (`researcher` above) is what `subAgents: [ "..." ]` references - it's purely a build-time wiring concern. * The subagent's own **declared `name`** (its agent definition's `name` field, e.g. `"ResearchBot"`) is what you retrieve it by at runtime - every agent in the tree (root + every subagent) is registered in `config/WireBox.bx` under this name, so a [`schedules/`](/conventions/schedules/index.html) scheduler reaches it with `agent( "ResearchBot" )` (and any other WireBox-aware code with a plain `getInstance( "ResearchBot" )`). These two names can differ, and often will - the folder name is an implementation detail, the declared `name` is the one that matters everywhere else (prompts, WireBox retrieval). Because it's now also a WireBox binding key, `build` fails validation if two agents in the tree - however deeply nested - end up with the same declared `name`, including two that both leave it unset and silently share the `"BxAi"` default.

# tests/

Every project scaffolded via `bxAgents new` gets a root [`box.json`](/conventions/box-json/index.html) (declaring `testbox` as a development dependency, installed into `lib/testbox`) and a ready-to-run `tests/` folder with `tests/specs/AgentSpec.bx`, an example spec that passes out of the box.

```bash
cd my-agent
box install       # fetches testbox into lib/testbox (new already ran this for you)
bxAgents test
```

> **Info**
>
> Inspired by the `coldbox-templates/boxlang` template's own dedicated `tests/` + `box.json` folder - adapted to BxAgents' own simpler testing story. Testing an agent is about its **behavior** (what it says, which tools it calls), not HTTP routing, so there's no `Application.bx`/ColdBox virtual app involved here at all.

## Writing a spec

Extend `bxModules.bxagents.models.testing.BaseAgentSpec` (a `testbox.system.BaseSpec` subclass) instead of `testbox.system.BaseSpec` directly:

```javascript
// tests/specs/AgentSpec.bx
class extends="bxModules.bxagents.models.testing.BaseAgentSpec" {

	function run() {
		describe( "my-agent", function() {

			it( "responds to a greeting", function() {
				mockResponses( [ "Hello! How can I help you today?" ] )

				var response = agent.run( "Hi there" )

				expect( response ).toContainText( "Hello" )
			} )

		} )
	}

}
```

`BaseAgentSpec` builds your agent once per spec bundle (`beforeAll()`), against a **throwaway temp copy** of your project - it never touches your real `.build/app`, so running tests never clobbers (or is clobbered by) a real `build`/`serve`/`package` cycle. The built agent is exposed as `agent`.

## Testing against the mock provider

By default, `bxAgents test` builds your agent using the `test` environment override in `Agent.yaml` (scaffolded automatically):

```yaml
# Agent.yaml
environments:
  test:
    model: mock/mock-model
```

A class-based `Agent.bx` expresses the same override as a `test()` method returning `{ model : "mock/mock-model" }`.

In the `test` environment every [profile](/conventions/models/index.html#profiles) is pointed at the `mock` provider too, so a project with profiles needs no key either.

This means your tests need **no API key and no network access** out of the box - the same `mock` provider convention used throughout BxAgents' own test suite. Edit this override if you want a spec to run against a real provider instead (you'll need a real API key available in the environment running the tests).

### `mockResponses( responses )`

Scripts the agent's next replies, consumed in order - one per LLM round-trip, including the intermediate turns of a tool-calling loop:

```javascript
mockResponses( [
	{ toolCalls: [ { name: "getWeather", arguments: { city: "Miami" } } ] },
	"It's sunny in Miami!"
] )

var response = agent.run( "What's the weather in Miami?" )
```

A plain string scripts a final reply. A `{ toolCalls: [ { name, arguments } ] }` struct scripts a tool-call turn - the named tool **actually executes for real** (against your real `tools/` implementation), and its real return value is what the next round-trip sees; only the LLM's own reply is scripted, never the tool's behavior.

## Custom matchers

`BaseAgentSpec` registers a few matchers, tailored to testing agent behavior, via TestBox's own `addMatchers()` extension point - use them exactly like any built-in TestBox matcher, including negation (`notTo...`):

|                Matcher                 |                                                                                      Checks                                                                                       |
|----------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `toContainText( "substring" )`         | The actual value (usually a response string) contains the given text, case-insensitively.                                                                                         |
| `toHaveCalledTool( "toolName" )`       | The agent's own recorded provider requests show it actually decided to invoke the named tool - not just that the tool exists.                                                     |
| `toHaveReceivedMessage( "substring" )` | Some message actually sent to the provider (any role, any round-trip) contained the given text - useful for asserting your system prompt/instructions actually reached the model. |

```javascript
expect( agent ).toHaveCalledTool( "getWeather" )
expect( agent ).notToHaveCalledTool( "getStockPrice" )
```

## Running tests

```bash
bxAgents test
```

Runs your project's `tests/specs/**` via TestBox, in a fresh child process (so it never fights over BoxLang's own class-mapping caches with anything else you're running). Prints bundle/suite/spec counts and pass/fail/error/skipped totals, plus one line per failure, and exits non-zero if anything failed - suitable as a CI gate before `deploy`.
> **Warning**
>
> `bxAgents test` requires TestBox actually installed in `lib/testbox` (`box install` in the project root; `tests/testbox` is also found, for projects scaffolded before `box.json` moved to the root) - it errors clearly, rather than silently reporting zero specs, if that hasn't been done yet.

title: The Build Pipeline
body:
The Build Pipeline bxAgents build runs a fixed sequence of phases, once, producing a plain ColdBox application. Nothing here runs again at request time - that's the whole point of build-time assembly. This page walks the phases in the exact order BuildPipeline.bx runs them. flowchart TD A["1 · Resolve config
AgentConfigResolver"] --> B["2 · Discover
ProjectDiscoverer"] B --> C{"3 · Validate
ProjectValidator"} C -->|"any error"| X["Build throws.
.build/app is never written or touched"] C -->|"clean
warnings never block"| D["4 · Generate"] D --> D1["1 Interceptors"] --> D2["2 Gateways"] --> D3["3 MCP"] --> D4["4 Router"] D4 --> D5["5 Agent API"] --> D6["6 Web UI"] --> D7["7 Extensions"] --> D8["8 Core app skeleton"] --> D9["9 Tools/skills copy"] D9 --> D10["10 Project modules"] --> D11["11 Runtime libraries"] --> D12["12 Scheduler"] D12 --> E["5 · Normalize + write
ManifestNormalizer"] E --> F[".build/manifest.json
+ .build/app - a plain ColdBox application"] style C fill:#fff3cd,stroke:#856404 style X fill:#f8d7da,stroke:#721c24 style F fill:#d4edda,stroke:#155724 Before phase 1, build restores any skill that .agents/skills.lock.json lists and the disk lacks, and any extension that extensions.lock.json lists and the disk lacks; a failed restore stops the build. Validation is the gate: it collects every error rather than failing fast, and nothing is generated until it comes back clean. (Packaging into a .bxa is a deliberately separate step - see Deployment & Secrets - so a fast build → inspect → build again loop never pays a packaging cost it doesn't need.) 1. Resolve config AgentConfigResolver loads the agent definition ( Agent.yaml , or the class-based Agent.bx ), applies the active environment's overrides (the environments: block of an Agent.yaml , or the override method and configure() of an Agent.bx ), then deep-merges in boxlang.json / boxlang-{env}.json / miniserver.json / miniserver-{env}.json if present. Produces the single resolved config struct every later phase reads from. 2. Discover ProjectDiscoverer walks the project root and enumerates every convention folder ( tools/ , skills/ and the registry's .agents/skills/ , subagents/ , gateways/ , mcp/ , interceptors/ , modules/ ) into raw { name, path, type } entries. schedules/*.bx are listed the same way, one entry per BoxLang scheduler file. Pure discovery - no interpretation of file contents happens yet. 3. Validate ProjectValidator runs every validator and collects every error (never fail-fast) plus any warnings: duplicate tool/skill/model/subagent names, duplicate agent name s across the whole subagent tree (see subagents/ ), circular subagent/module references, the two gateway entry shapes, remote MCP config completeness, and model/provider validity. If any errors were collected, the build throws immediately here - no .build/app is written or touched. Warnings (e.g. a schedules/ folder with no Scheduler.bx in it) never block the build. 4. Generate Only reached once validation is clean. Any .build/app from an earlier build is deleted first. In order: Interceptors - InterceptorSplitter copies agent -scope interceptors into .build/app/interceptors , runtime -scope ones into a separate .build/runtime-interceptors directory, outside the app (BxAgents does not register those for you). Gateways - GatewayGenerator emits aiGatewayRegistry().register(...) statements for channel-adapter entries, and writes a small .build/app/handlers/*.bx webhook handler for each whatsapp-cloud , teams , twilio or github entry. If any entry is a push-style gateway (e.g. type: "telegram" ), it also produces the start-up statement that builds a single bx-ai GatewaySession (bundling every push-style gateway) bound to the project's root agent. MCP - McpGenerator copies local mcp/* servers into .build/app/mcp and emits their mcpServer(...).registerTool(...) registration statements. Router - RouterGenerator writes .build/app/config/Router.bx : the reserved /__bxagents agent API (at agentApi.path , unless agentApi.enabled is false ), the same four turn routes under the path of each exposes: "agent" entry, one route(path).toMCP(...) per exposes: "mcp" entry, the cbSecurity middleware for agentApi.allowedIPs and agentApi.rateLimit when set, a single route("/gateways").toAiGateway() if the project has any channel-adapter gateway, and one webhook route per whatsapp-cloud (GET+POST), teams , twilio or github push-style gateway present. Agent API - AgentApiGenerator writes .build/app/handlers/AgentApi.bx , every action of the agent API ( invoke , stream , batch , info , and the run-control, conversation, notes, command and token actions such as events , cancel , steer , resume , sessions and command ), all served by the one handler. Skipped when agentApi.enabled is false . Web UI - WebUiGenerator runs for any exposes: "webui" entry, writing the static /index.html (a client of the agent API , so no handler of its own), models/ChatDb.bx (the sign-in accounts and the store's forward-only migrations, built at boot by a start-up statement rather than on whichever request touches the database first) and the user models ( User , UserService , PasswordHasher ). apiKeyEnvVar becomes the agent API's shared secret. When users are declared it also writes the account seeder, interceptors/WebUiLoginGate.bx and handlers/ChatAuth.bx . It returns the resolved database config, which the next step needs. Extensions - ExtensionsGenerator copies the project's extensions/ folder to .build/app/extensions and writes config/extensions.json from the extensions: block of Agent.yaml , so the served agent loads them. Skipped when there is no extensions/ folder. Core app skeleton - ColdBoxAppGenerator writes the generated base bxagents/Application.bx (the wiring, see Application.bx ), the app's Application.bx (your root one copied as it is, or a plain one that extends the base), bxagents/Scheduler.bx , config/ColdBox.bx , config/WireBox.bx , agent/GeneratedAgentFactory.bx , and index.bxm , threading in every statement gathered above (gateway registrations, the GatewaySession start, MCP registrations, the web UI's store warm-up and account seeding, and - if tools/ has any files - a bare aiToolRegistry().scan("tools") call) into the base's onApplicationStart() . Interceptors are registered there too, one getInterceptorService().register(...) per agent-scope interceptor and web UI gate: a declarative interceptors array in config/ColdBox.bx never reaches ColdBox's interceptor service, so the generated config declares none. Every generated agent also now always receives a checkpointer ( withCheckpointer(...) , defaulting to a cache -backed aiMemory() if the project declares no checkpointer config and the class set none of its own) - without one, human-in-the-loop approval flows through any gateway other than cli fail outright. config/WireBox.bx maps every agent in the tree (root + every subagent) under its own declared name , not just the fixed root "GeneratedAgent" alias - see schedules/ . Each agent node's instructions.md is copied into the app as part of this step, mirroring the source layout under agent/ - the root project's to .build/app/agent/instructions.md , each subagent's to .build/app/agent/subagents//instructions.md - so every node keeps its own and the built app carries the file it reads at runtime. The factory reads all three of its runtime paths ( instructions.md , its own tools/ , and any class-based agent's copied Agent.bx ) through a small generated resolveAppPath() helper that resolves them relative to the factory's own location on disk, falling back to the build-time absolute path if that self-location doesn't resolve - which is what makes a packaged .bxa genuinely relocatable rather than runnable only on the machine that built it. For a project with a webui exposure it also turns session management on, registers the SQLite datasource (naming it as the app default via this.datasource ), creates the database's parent directory in onApplicationStart() - SQLite creates the file but never the folder holding it - and pins qb's grammar in config/ColdBox.bx . Tools/skills copy - ToolsSkillsCopier wipes and rewrites .build/app/tools and .build/app/skills verbatim from your project's own folders, adding the registry skills from .agents/skills/ to the app's skills/ . Project modules - BoxLangModulesCopier copies the BoxLang modules installed in the project's boxlang_modules/ into .build/app/boxlang_modules , leaving out any that box.json lists only as a development dependency. Skipped when there is no boxlang_modules/ folder. Runtime libraries - RuntimeLibsCopier copies the ColdBox runtime bundled inside BxAgents into .build/app : coldbox/ plus modules/qb , modules/cbsecurity , modules/cbauth , modules/cbmailservices and their dependencies. A lib/ folder in your project (same layout) is copied afterwards and wins, which is how you add or override a library. The bundled copy exists only in an installed or built module, so a source checkout skips this step with a warning. Schedulers - SchedulerGenerator copies each schedules/*.bx to .build/app/schedules/.bx , adding extends="bxagents.Scheduler" to a class that names no parent. The base Application already lists them in this.schedulers , so BoxLang starts them with the app. 5. Normalize + write the manifest ManifestNormalizer produces the canonical, hash-stamped internal manifest from the discovery + resolved-config data, and the pipeline writes it to .build/manifest.json . Idempotency Rebuilding an unchanged project produces byte-identical output, down to the manifest's per-file content hashes - the entire point of paying the assembly cost once, at build time, rather than deferring any of this work into request handling.

Each agent node's `instructions.md` is **copied into the app** as part of this step, mirroring the source layout under `agent/` - the root project's to `.build/app/agent/instructions.md`, each subagent's to `.build/app/agent/subagents//instructions.md` - so every node keeps its own and the built app carries the file it reads at runtime. The factory reads all three of its runtime paths (`instructions.md`, its own `tools/`, and any class-based agent's copied `Agent.bx`) through a small generated `resolveAppPath()` helper that resolves them relative to the factory's own location on disk, falling back to the build-time absolute path if that self-location doesn't resolve - which is what makes a packaged `.bxa` genuinely relocatable rather than runnable only on the machine that built it. For a project with a `webui` exposure it also turns session management on, registers the SQLite datasource (naming it as the app default via `this.datasource`), creates the database's parent directory in `onApplicationStart()` - SQLite creates the file but never the folder holding it - and pins qb's grammar in `config/ColdBox.bx`. 9. **Tools/skills copy** - `ToolsSkillsCopier` wipes and rewrites `.build/app/tools` and `.build/app/skills` verbatim from your project's own folders, adding the registry skills from `.agents/skills/` to the app's `skills/`. 10. **Project modules** - `BoxLangModulesCopier` copies the BoxLang modules installed in the project's `boxlang_modules/` into `.build/app/boxlang_modules`, leaving out any that `box.json` lists only as a development dependency. Skipped when there is no `boxlang_modules/` folder. 11. **Runtime libraries** - `RuntimeLibsCopier` copies the ColdBox runtime bundled inside BxAgents into `.build/app`: `coldbox/` plus `modules/qb`, `modules/cbsecurity`, `modules/cbauth`, `modules/cbmailservices` and their dependencies. A `lib/` folder in your project (same layout) is copied afterwards and wins, which is how you add or override a library. The bundled copy exists only in an installed or built module, so a source checkout skips this step with a warning. 12. **Schedulers** - [`SchedulerGenerator`](/conventions/schedules/index.html) copies each `schedules/*.bx` to `.build/app/schedules/.bx`, adding `extends="bxagents.Scheduler"` to a class that names no parent. The base `Application` already lists them in `this.schedulers`, so BoxLang starts them with the app. ## 5. Normalize + write the manifest [`ManifestNormalizer`](/manifest/index.html) produces the canonical, hash-stamped internal manifest from the discovery + resolved-config data, and the pipeline writes it to `.build/manifest.json`. ## Idempotency Rebuilding an unchanged project produces byte-identical output, down to the manifest's per-file content hashes - the entire point of paying the assembly cost once, at build time, rather than deferring any of this work into request handling.

# The Manifest

Every `build` writes `.build/manifest.json` - BxAgents' own record of exactly what went into the generated app. `bxAgents inspect` reports whether a project was built and the manifest's version and file count in its `build` section (the manifest itself is a plain file you can open); `bxAgents package` copies a **redacted** version of it alongside the `.bxa` (see [Deployment \& Secrets](/deployment-and-secrets/index.html)).

## Schema

```json
{
	"manifestVersion": "1.0.0",
	"generator": { "name": "bx-agents", "version": "dev" },
	"agent": {
		"name": "my-agent",
		"description": "",
		"model": "openai/gpt-5",
		"environment": "development"
	},
	"files": [
		{ "category": "tools", "name": "Greeter", "path": "tools/Greeter.bx", "hash": "..." }
	]
}
```

|                 Field                  |                                                                                                                                                                                         Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                          |
|----------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `manifestVersion`                      | Semver stamp for the manifest schema itself (currently `1.0.0`) - `package` refuses to run if this is unset or malformed.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `generator.name` / `generator.version` | Always `"bx-agents"` / the version string stamped into the build: `dev` unless `bxAgents build --generatorVersion=...` says otherwise.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `agent`                                | Only safe, structural fields (`name`, `description`, `model`, `environment`) - **never** secrets. For a class-based `Agent.bx` that sets them in code, `name`, `description` and `model` are read from the class. Secrets are never read into the manifest at all; they're resolved by bx-ai itself, live, at runtime.                                                                   |
| `files`                                | One entry per discovered convention-folder item, each `{ category, name, path, hash }`. The categories are `tools`, `skills` (your own and the ones installed from the registry), `subagents`, `gateways`, `schedules` (one per scheduler file), `mcp`, `interceptors` and `modules`. Sorted by category then path for deterministic ordering - independent of filesystem listing order. |

## Content hashes

Each `files[]` entry's `hash` is a SHA-256 of its content:

* **A file**: the hash of its content, with line endings normalized first (CRLF and LF checkouts of the same content hash identically).
* **A directory** (a skill folder, a subagent folder, a module folder): the hash of every contained file's own `relativePath:contentHash`, recursively, sorted for determinism - so renaming or editing any single file inside changes the whole folder's hash.

This is what makes rebuilding an unchanged project produce an **identical** manifest: same categories, same ordering, same hashes, every time - and it's exactly why changing one tool file's content only ever changes that one entry's hash, nothing else.

## Compatibility policy

`manifestVersion` exists so a future breaking change to this schema can be detected by anything reading `manifest.json` (a deploy target, a future `inspect` version, external tooling) - a tool encountering an unrecognized major version should refuse to guess at the shape and fail clearly, rather than silently misreading fields.

markdown:
# The new wizard

Run `bxAgents new` in a terminal with no `--model` and it asks what the agent should do, then writes the project to match. Nothing in it is magic: every answer ends up in a file you can read, and the last screen prints the one-line command that would build the same project without any questions.

```bash
bxAgents new my-agent
```

It is a full-screen UI in the teal of the BxAgents logo. Arrow keys (or `j`/`k`) move, Space ticks, Enter confirms, **Esc goes back one question** , **Ctrl+C cancels** and creates nothing. Answers you have given collapse to one line each above the current question.

*The whole wizard in one run: a single agent on OpenAI with web search, memory saved to disk and a web chat.*

![The wizard's second question](/assets/tui/wizard-name.png)

*Answers you have given collapse to one line each above the question.*

## What it asks

|      Stage      |                                                                                                           What you choose                                                                                                            |                                                                    What it writes                                                                    |
|-----------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Name, purpose   | The agent's name and a one-line description                                                                                                                                                                                          | `name`, `description` in [`Agent.yaml`](/conventions/agent-yaml/index.html)                                                                          |
| Shape           | A single agent, a team, a scheduled agent, an MCP server                                                                                                                                                                             | The matching [template](/agent-templates/index.html)                                                                                                 |
| Model           | A provider, then optionally a model name (Enter takes the provider's default). **Another provider** lets you type `provider/model` yourself                                                                                          | `model`, and a stub for the provider's `<PROVIDER>_API_KEY` in `.env`                                                                                |
| Model settings  | Whether to tune the model, then the temperature (0 to 2), the longest answer in tokens and the timeout in seconds. Enter leaves one unset                                                                                            | [`params`](/conventions/models/index.html) (`temperature`, `max_tokens`) and [`options`](/conventions/models/index.html) (`timeout`) in `Agent.yaml` |
| Tools           | Date and time, fetch pages, search the web, browse websites, files, images, speech and translation                                                                                                                                   | A [`tools:`](/conventions/agent-yaml/index.html#tools) list; browsing also adds `bx-playwright` to your `box.json`                                   |
| Search provider | The built-in one, Brave, Tavily, Exa or Google                                                                                                                                                                                       | A key stub in `.env`, and a line in `instructions.md` telling the agent which provider to use                                                        |
| File tools      | Read only, all 19, or tool by tool, then the folders they may use                                                                                                                                                                    | [`toolOptions.bxai.allowedPaths`](/conventions/agent-yaml/index.html#file-tools)                                                                     |
| Memory          | In memory, or saved to disk                                                                                                                                                                                                          | `memory` and `checkpointer`                                                                                                                          |
| MCP servers     | GitHub, Stripe, Notion, Atlassian, Cloudflare, Supabase, Git                                                                                                                                                                         | [`mcpServers`](/conventions/mcp/index.html#consuming-remote-servers) entries and token stubs                                                         |
| Channels        | Web chat, HTTP API, Telegram, Slack, Discord, WhatsApp, Teams, SMS, GitHub, Email, Signal                                                                                                                                            | A `gateways/*.bx` file and the stubs it needs                                                                                                        |
| Web access      | Open, a shared key, or named users with passwords                                                                                                                                                                                    | `apiKeyEnvVar` or `users` on the web chat entry                                                                                                      |
| Guard           | Flag or block suspicious input, or turn the guard off                                                                                                                                                                                | A [`security`](/conventions/agent-yaml/index.html#settings) block                                                                                    |
| Look and feel   | The terminal chat's prompt style (bars, bars-hints, rule, box or panel), then the widgets for the top bar and for the bottom (agent, profile, folder, user, clock, machine, git, date, session, elapsed, `ctx` for the context size) | A [`tui:`](/conventions/agent-yaml/index.html#settings) block, written only when you change something                                                |
| Deploy          | Docker, DigitalOcean, SSH, SFTP, FTP, a local folder, or later                                                                                                                                                                       | `deploy/<target>.json`                                                                                                                               |
| Review          | A summary of every answer and the one-line command that repeats it. Choose **Create the project** , **Start over** or **Cancel**                                                                                                     | Nothing until you create                                                                                                                             |

A stage whose answer you already gave as a flag is skipped and shown as answered. A stage that does not apply (the search provider when search is off) is skipped without a word.

![The search provider question](/assets/tui/wizard-search.png)

*A stage appears only when an earlier answer needs it: ticking web search asks which provider.*

![The question for the top bar widgets](/assets/tui/wizard-widgets.png)

*The look-and-feel stage previews each widget with a sample value.*

## File tools never get the whole disk

bx-ai ships 19 file tools but registers none of them. The wizard offers them, and always asks **which folders** they may use: the temp folder (`tmp`), the folder you run the agent from (`cwd`), or a path you type. It will not continue with none. There is no way to ask for unrestricted access from the wizard or from the flags; an empty list is refused because bx-ai reads an empty list as "everywhere".

```yaml
tools:
  - readFile@bxai
  - listDirectory@bxai
toolOptions:
  bxai:
    allowedPaths:
      - tmp
      - cwd
```

## Secrets

The wizard never asks you to type a secret that it stores.

* **API keys and tokens** go in `.env` as empty stubs, each under a comment saying where to get it. The files that use them hold only the variable's **name**.
* A **web access key** is generated for you (a random 64-character value) and written to `.env`, because it protects something you are about to run.
* A **web chat password** is hashed with the same PBKDF2 hasher as `bxAgents hash-password`; only the hash reaches `gateways/webui.bx`, and it is safe to commit.

`.env` is in the `.gitignore` the project is created with.

## MCP servers

All servers in the picker are remote (HTTP) servers that the bundled bx-ai can connect to, listed with how risky they are. Each starts with its credential read from the environment when the app starts:

```yaml
mcpServers:
  - name: github
    url: "https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/"
    token: "${env.GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

|   Server   |           Credential           |                                    Risk                                    |
|------------|--------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| GitHub     | `GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN` | High: can open and merge pull requests, push files, trigger Actions        |
| Stripe     | `STRIPE_AGENT_API_KEY`         | High: moves money. Use a sandbox account first                             |
| Notion     | `NOTION_MCP_TOKEN`             | Medium: edits and deletes pages. Tokens need a Business or Enterprise plan |
| Atlassian  | `ATLASSIAN_API_TOKEN`          | Medium. Unverified: the header an API token goes in is not documented      |
| Cloudflare | `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`         | High: DNS, Workers, billable resources, depending on the token             |
| Supabase   | `SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN`        | High: runs SQL. The address starts read-only                               |

Picking a high-risk server shows what it can do before you continue. **Git** runs as a program on your machine (`uvx mcp-server-git`), so it needs [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) installed where the agent runs, and it works in the folder you start the agent from. The wizard writes it as a `command` entry; see [programs as MCP servers](/conventions/mcp/index.html#servers-that-run-as-a-program).

## After it is created

![The final screen after the project is created](/assets/tui/wizard-done.png)

*The last screen: where the project is, what to do next, and the command that repeats it without questions.*

`new` runs `box install` (skip it with `--skipInstall`), then prints what is left: the keys to fill in, how to chat, test, serve and deploy, and, for each channel you chose, the setup that happens outside the project. For WhatsApp that means the Meta app, the verify token and a public address; for Slack, Socket Mode and two tokens; for Signal, a running `signal-cli`. The same steps live on each [gateway page](/conventions/gateways/index.html).

## Without the wizard

The wizard writes nothing a flag cannot. The last screen prints the command; this one came from a real run:

```bash
bxAgents new support-bot --name=support-bot --model=claude --with=time,fetch,search --search=brave \
  --mcp=github --channels=web,telegram --web-auth=key --guard=flag --deploy=docker --registry=ghcr:me/support-bot
```

|              Flag               |                                                                                                        Takes                                                                                                         |
|---------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `--with`                        | `time`, `fetch`, `search`, `browse`, `files`, `media` (a list)                                                                                                                                                       |
| `--search`                      | `http`, `brave`, `tavily`, `exa`, `google`                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `--files`, `--files-dir`        | `read`, `all` or a list of tool names; folders as `tmp`, `cwd` or absolute paths. Both are needed together                                                                                                           |
| `--temperature`                 | A number from 0 to 2                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `--max-tokens`, `--timeout`     | A positive whole number (tokens, seconds)                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `--memory`                      | `cache` or `file`                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `--mcp`                         | MCP server ids (a list)                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `--channels`                    | `web`, `api`, or channel ids (a list)                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `--web-auth`                    | `open` or `key`. Users need passwords, so they come from the wizard or from `gateways/webui.bx`                                                                                                                      |
| `--guard`                       | `off`, `flag` or `block`                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `--prompt`                      | `bars`, `bars-hints`, `rule`, `box` or `panel`                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `--widgets`, `--widgets-bottom` | Widget names for the top bar and for the bottom (a list), or `none`                                                                                                                                                  |
| `--deploy`                      | `docker`, `digitalocean`, `ssh`, `sftp`, `ftp`, `local`, with `--registry=ghcr:owner/name` (or `dockerhub:`, `docr:`), `--app`, `--region`, `--host`, `--user`, `--remote-path`, `--destination` as the target needs |

A flag with a bad value stops the command and says what the flag accepts. The wizard turns on when:

|                   You run                    |                                        Result                                        |
|----------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `bxAgents new` at a terminal                 | The full-screen wizard                                                               |
| `bxAgents new` in a pipe, or with `--no-tui` | The same questions as numbered lines. Type `back` to go back                         |
| `bxAgents new --model=...`                   | No questions: a model means a script is calling. Add `--wizard` to be asked the rest |
| `bxAgents new --no-wizard` or `--yes`        | No questions, flags and defaults only                                                |

Set `NO_COLOR` for plain output. The Agent.yaml options the wizard writes need the default `Agent.yaml`, so they cannot be combined with `--class`.

title: The terminal UI
body: The terminal UI Two commands draw a full terminal screen: bxAgents chat , where you talk to your agent, and bxAgents new , where you answer questions and get a project. This page is the tour. Every command and flag is in the CLI reference ; every slash command is in Slash commands ; a guided first session is in Chat walkthroughs . A chat session: slash commands, a tool call and a formatted answer. The answers in these recordings come from a scripted demo model, so they are canned. Everything else is the real screen. Start a chat bxAgents build # chat needs a built agent (not with --connect) bxAgents chat Run Talks to Use it when bxAgents chat The agent, loaded in this process You want to talk to the agent. Fastest. bxAgents chat --server A throwaway local server You need interceptors, schedules or gateways to be real bxAgents chat --connect=<url> [--token=<t>] A server that is already running You want to talk to a deployment bxAgents chat --no-tui Same as the first, in a plain line-by-line prompt A terminal that cannot draw, or you just prefer it --continue reopens your latest conversation, --session=<number or id> a particular one, --user=<name> chooses whose conversations and notes you see. The screen Finished turns are printed as ordinary terminal text, so your scrollback, search and copy keep working . Only two things are redrawn: the message box at the bottom and the answer being written. Answers stream in as they are produced and are printed as formatted Markdown when complete: headings, lists, tables with rounded borders, and code blocks coloured by language. Tool calls are shown with their arguments and how long they took. Thinking is shown while the model works and is never kept. Approvals. When a run stops for a human-in-the-loop decision, the screen asks in place: approve once, approve for the conversation, or reject.
